			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 1.&nbsp;&nbsp;BUSINES<a name="ITEM1BUSINESS_207175"></a>S</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Introduction</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Almost Family,&nbsp;Inc. </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;font-size:6.5pt;">TM</font><font style="display:inline;"> and subsidiaries (collectively &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Almost Family</font><font style="display:inline;">&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;) is a leading provider of cost efficient, high quality home healthcare services and related innovations to drive savings for payors and improve patient outcomes and experience.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Company, founded in 1976, operates over 340 locations across 26 states.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unless otherwise indicated, the financial information included in Part&nbsp;I is for continuing operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Website Access to Our Reports</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our annual reports on Form&nbsp;10-K, quarterly reports on Form&nbsp;10-Q, current reports on Form&nbsp;8-K, and all amendments to those reports are available free of charge on our website at www.almostfamily.com as soon as reasonably practicable after such material is electronically filed with or furnished to the SEC.&nbsp;&nbsp;Information contained on Almost Family&#x2019;s website is not part of this annual report on Form&nbsp;10-K and is not incorporated by reference in this document.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">How We Are Currently Organized and Operate</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has two divisions, Home Health and Healthcare Innovations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Home Health division is comprised of two reportable segments, Visiting Nurse Services (&#x201C;VN&#x201D; or &#x201C;Visiting Nurse&#x201D;) and Personal Care Services (&#x201C;PC&#x201D; or &#x201C;Personal Care&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Healthcare Innovations is also a reporting segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reportable segments have been identified based upon how management has organized the business by services provided to customers and the criteria in Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) Topic 280, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Segment Reporting</font><font style="display:inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;All references herein for the years 2016, 2015 and 2014 represent the fiscal years ended December 30, 2016 and January 1, 2016, and the calendar year ended December 31, 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our VN segment provides a comprehensive range of Medicare-certified home health nursing services to patients in need of recuperative care, typically following a period of hospitalization or care in another type of inpatient facility. Our services are often provided to patients in lieu of additional care in other settings, such as long term acute care hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation hospitals or skilled nursing facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our nurses, therapists, medical social workers and home health aides work closely with patients and their families to design and implement an individualized treatment response to a physician-prescribed plan of care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the umbrella of our &#x201C;Senior Advocacy&#x201D; mission, we offer special clinically-based protocols customized to meet the needs of the increasingly medically complex, chronic and co-morbid patient populations we serve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Examples include Optimum Balance, Silver Steps, Cardiocare, Orthopedic and Conjestive Heart Failure in the Home.&nbsp;&nbsp;VN Medicare revenues are generated on a per episode basis rather than a fee per visit or hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 95% of the VN segment revenues are generated from the Medicare program while the balance is generated from Medicaid and private insurance programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our PC segment provides services in patients&#x2019; homes primarily on an as-needed, hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;These services include personal care, medication management, meal preparation, caregiver respite and homemaking. Our services are often provided to patients who would otherwise be admitted to skilled nursing facilities for long term custodial care.&nbsp;&nbsp;PC revenues are generated on an hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 83% of the PC segment revenues are generated from Medicaid and other government programs while the balance is generated from insurance programs and private pay patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Healthcare Innovations (&#x201C;HCI&#x201D;) segment includes our developmental activity outside of the traditional home health business platform.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Additional financial information about our segments can be found in Part&nbsp;II,&nbsp;Item 8, &#x201C;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#x201D; and related notes included elsewhere in this Form 10-K.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Our View on Reimbursement and Diversification of Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our Company is highly dependent on government reimbursement programs which pay for the majority of the services we provide to our patients and customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reimbursement under these programs, primarily Medicare and Medicaid, is subject to frequent changes as policy makers balance constituents&#x2019; needs for health care services within the constraints of the specific government&#x2019;s fiscal budget.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare and Medicaid, respectively, are consuming a greater percentage of federal and states&#x2019; budgets, which is exacerbated in times of economic downturn.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that these financial issues are cyclical in nature rather than indicative of the long-term prospect for Medicare and Medicaid funding of health care services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we believe our services offer the lowest cost alternative to institutional care and are a part of the solution to the federal government&#x2019;s Medicare and states&#x2019; Medicaid financing problems.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We believe that an important key to our historical success and to our future success is our ability to adapt our operations to meet changes in reimbursement as they occur.&nbsp;&nbsp;One important way in which we have achieved this adaptability in the past, and in which we plan to achieve it in the future, is to maintain some level of diversification in our business mix.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The execution of our business plan will place primary emphasis on the development of our home health operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;As our business grows, we may evaluate opportunities for the provision of other health care services in patients&#x2019; homes that would be consistent with our Senior Advocacy mission.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Our Business Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our future success depends on our ability to execute our business plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the next three to five years we will try to accomplish the following:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Generate meaningful same store sales growth through the focused provision of high quality services and attending to the needs of our patients;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Drive our costs down, while continuing to provide high quality patient care, by improving the productivity of our work force through improved monitoring, tighter controls, workflow automation, use of technology and other opportunities for efficiency gains;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Expand the significance of our home health services by selectively acquiring other quality providers, through the startup of new agencies and potentially by providing new services in patients&#x2019; homes consistent with our Senior Advocacy mission;</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>

		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Make additional strategic investments which expand our Healthcare Innovation segment in its mission to find solutions for more effective, efficient and appropriate delivery of homecare; and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Symbol;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Overview of Our Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Home Health Division Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Acquisition of Home Health and Hospice Segment of Community Health Systems</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December&nbsp;31, 2016, the first day after our 2016 fiscal year end, we completed the acquisition of the home health segment of Community Health Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (&#x201C;CHS&#x201D; and &#x201C;CHS JV Transaction&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Community Health Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (NYSE: CYH) is one of the largest publicly-traded hospital companies in the United States and a leading operator of general acute care hospitals in communities across the country.&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS Home Health, which includes the former home health and hospice operations of CHS, provides in-home outpatient care services, including skilled nursing and acute care. CHS Home Health's operations are located primarily in the Midwest and Southern United States with a major presence in Tennessee, Florida and Texas near existing CHS hospitals.&nbsp;&nbsp;The home health business consists of 74 separate </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">5</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">home health agencies across 22 states and the hospice business consists of 15 separate hospice agencies across 7 states.&nbsp;&nbsp;We currently anticipate reporting the results of the JV as part of our Home Health division.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The CHS Home Health transaction is structured as a joint venture (the "JV") with Almost Family owning 80% and CHS retaining a 20% stake. The JV is maintained and managed by Almost Family as a separate legal entity with a separate line-management organization, led by CHS' former home health management team. Almost Family provides a full-range of home office management services under an ever-green management services agreement and, in return, receives a management fee of 5% of the JV's annual revenue. The JV operations management team remains in-place in Franklin, TN, in order to provide continuity. With the exception of the separate management team that runs day-to-day operations, the JV will receive the support and integration of our home office functions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In addition to the JV operating agreement between CHS and Almost Family, CHS entered into affiliation and license agreements with the JV. The affiliation agreement provides for continued affiliation between the CHS hospitals and the home health agencies with a particular focus on care-coordination for the benefit of patients and referral sources who choose to use the JV agencies for their home health and hospice needs. The license agreement permits each home health agency to continue to operate under the CHS hospital tradenames to maintain cohesive presentation to the marketplace as part of the hospitals' post-acute care continuum.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">CHS Home Health has a board of five managers, four appointed by Almost Family and one appointed by CHS. Certain matters, including the sale of the business, acquisitions by CHS Home Health, change of business lines and annual operating budgets, among others, will require "super-majority" approval. CHS Home Health's Operating Agreement includes a dispute resolution process, ending in binding arbitration if necessary to break deadlocks. Almost Family will fund the working capital (subject to certain limits) needs of CHS Home Health, and any amounts outstanding at CHS Home Health or intercompany loans must be repaid before any distributions to owners can be made.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Visiting Nurse Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our VN segment provides a comprehensive range of Medicare-certified home health nursing services to patients in need of recuperative health care, typically following a period of hospitalization or care in another type of inpatient facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our patients are referred to us by their physicians or upon discharge from a hospital or other type of in-patient facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;After the CHS JV Transaction, our VN segment operates 242 Medicare-certified home health agencies and 16 hospice branches for a total of 258 locations.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated 70% of our revenues for 2016, of which approximately 95% were derived from the Medicare program.&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our Visiting Nurse segment provides a comprehensive range of Medicare-certified home health nursing services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We receive payment from Medicare, Medicaid and private insurance companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our professional staff includes registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, physical, speech and occupational therapists, and medical social workers.&nbsp;&nbsp;They fulfill medical treatment plans prescribed by physicians.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our professional staff is subject to state licensing requirements in the particular states in which they practice.&nbsp;&nbsp;Para-professional staff members (primarily home health aides) also provide care to these patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our Visiting Nurse segment operations located in Florida normally experience higher admissions during the first quarter and lower admissions during the third quarter than in the other quarters due to seasonal population fluctuations.&nbsp;&nbsp;VN segment operations located in Florida generated approximately 26% of our revenue for 2016.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Personal Care Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our PC segment services are also provided in patients&#x2019; homes on an as needed hourly basis, including personal care, medication management, meal preparation, caregiver respite and homemaking.&nbsp;&nbsp;These services (generally provided by para-professional staff such as home health aides) are generally of a custodial rather than skilled nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, PC revenues are generated on an hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;We currently operate 82 Personal Care locations.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated 26% of our revenues for 2016, of which approximately 83% were derived from the Medicaid program.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Healthcare Innovations Segment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our HCI business segment was created to house and separately report on our developmental activities outside our traditional home health business platform.&nbsp;&nbsp;These activities are intended ultimately, whether directly or indirectly, to benefit our patients and payers through the enhanced provision of home health services.&nbsp;&nbsp;HCI activities all share a common goal of improving patient experiences and quality outcomes, while lowering costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;These include, but are not limited to: technology, information, population health management, risk-sharing, assessments, care coordination and transitions, clinical advancements, enhanced patient engagement and informed clinical decision making.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe these activities help us discover valuable insight and experiences that would not otherwise be gained in the routine operation of our core home health business segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, we believe these innovation activities will play an important role in collaborating with policy makers, payers, providers, and anyone who assumes financial risk for managing patient populations, to seek to reduce costs, and improve quality by providing increasingly more care for more patients in their homes than ever before.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated approximately 4% of our revenue for 2016.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As discussed further below, the HCI segment currently includes: a)&nbsp;Imperium Health Management,&nbsp;LLC ("Imperium"), an ACO enablement company, b)&nbsp;an investment in NavHealth,&nbsp;Inc. ("NavHealth"), a population-health analytics company, c)&nbsp;Ingenios Health&nbsp;Co. ("Ingenios"), a Nurse-Practitioner-oriented and mobile technology-enabled health risk assessment company primarily serving managed care organizations; and d)&nbsp;Long Term Solutions,&nbsp;Inc. ("LTS"), an in-home assessment company serving the long-term care insurance industry.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Some of these initiatives are highly speculative and have been made in development stage enterprises.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that we will receive any return on, or of, the capital we invest in these ventures.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, we believe these activities already have, and will continue to help us, discover valuable insights and experiences we would not otherwise gain in the routine operation of our core home health business segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;These endeavors are part of a growing number of care-related innovations and reforms.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect more will be attempted over the next several years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Imperium</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Imperium's purpose is to assist independent primary care physician practices in establishing and successfully operating Accountable Care Organizations ("ACOs") first made possible by 2010's Affordable Care Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;Through improved care management, in a coordinated effort led by primary care physicians, with nurses and home health agencies using evidence-based clinical standards, we seek to reduce avoidable hospitalizations, emergent care, and non-impactful health care services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We seek to work together with primary care physicians to manage high-cost patients in lower-cost settings, with a goal of generating, and sharing in, savings to the Medicare program.&nbsp;&nbsp;By linking physicians with home health care through the ACO vehicle we seek to deliver meaningful savings to the healthcare system and participate in a </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">8</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">share of those savings under the Medicare Shared Savings Program ("MSSP") and such other similar models as may evolve in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Imperium has rapidly expanded its customer base growing from 3 ACOs under contract in 2013, to 7 in 2014, 11 in 2015, 14 in 2016 and 15 in 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;In terms of covered Medicare beneficiaries, Imperium has grown from 23,000 in 2013, to 45,000 in 2014 and 85,000 in 2015, 124,000 in 2016 and now has 142,000 in 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we intend to work together toward the development of additional ACO relationships in markets in which Almost Family also provides home health services, Imperium also currently has, and will continue to seek, ACO customers in other service territories.&nbsp;&nbsp;We own 72% of Imperium and consolidate its result in our financial statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;We report a provision for noncontrolling interests (&#x201C;NCI&#x201D;) to reflect the income or losses attributable to the 28% interest that we do not own.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">CMS announced the first year financial reconciliation and quality performance results for ACOs in September of 2014, in which, fifty-three ACOs generated shared savings during their first performance year ended December&nbsp;31, 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;ACOs that generated savings earned a performance payment, if they met the quality standard.&nbsp;&nbsp;CMS announced the third year results in August of 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;Imperium serviced ACOs have received an MSSP payments in the first, second, and third CMS results.&nbsp;&nbsp;Imperium received its share of $4.3&nbsp;million in 2016 for 2015 services, $1.4&nbsp;million in 2015 for 2014 services and $1.6&nbsp;million in 2014 for 2013 services.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that future payments will be made by CMS, the structure of MSSP payments will remain as currently deployed, or that an MSSP payment will be received in 2017 related to our 2016 services or any future period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent: -10pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Long Term Solutions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January&nbsp;5, 2016, we acquired Long Term Solutions,&nbsp;Inc.&nbsp;&nbsp;See "Acquisitions" for additional information.&nbsp;&nbsp;LTS performs in-home nursing assessments for the long-term care insurance industry. LTS also provides a suite of planning and support services to insurance companies, employers and direct to individuals and families throughout the United States. LTS, through its network of thousands of assessment service partners provides assessments in all 50 U.S. states and a number of foreign countries. LTS estimates that the majority of its assessments result in the patient ultimately receiving home health, assisted living or skilled nursing care in accordance with their long-term care insurance benefits.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:11.25pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance ("AALTCI") estimates that the industry paid over $7.5&nbsp;billion in claims covering 273,000 beneficiaries across the US in its most recently studied year and that over two-thirds of all newly-opened long term care insurance claims paid for care in the home or in an assisted living community setting.&nbsp;&nbsp;The AALTCI also reported total benefit payments increased by 13&nbsp;percent and the number of long term care insurance policyholders on claim grew 3.4&nbsp;percent.&nbsp;&nbsp;According to the National Association of Insurance Commissioners ("NAIC") the top 100 plans in the US cover 7.2&nbsp;million lives.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Ingenios Health Co.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Ingenios is a provider of technology enabled in-home clinical assessments for Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial Exchange lives in four states and Washington, D.C.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe new health assessment capabilities provide the key element in the evolution of improved care planning and delivery as healthcare delivery and reimbursement models evolve.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">NavHealth</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">NavHealth is a development-stage enterprise whose business plan is focused on the development of technology-based tools designed to help health systems anticipate and inform a patient&#x2019;s journey through the health care system.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among its other objectives, NavHealth seeks to develop and market a software platform designed to assist health care providers, managed care organizations and insurers in their efforts to aggregate patient data from various sources, improve patient engagement, satisfaction and outcomes and lower the overall cost of healthcare delivery.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are co-invested in NavHealth with founders Aneesh Chopra and Hunch Analytics which Chopra co-founded with Sanju Bansal.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Bansal is the co-founder and former COO of MicroStrategy (MSTR), a worldwide provider of enterprise software for cloud business intelligence and big data services.&nbsp;&nbsp;We made an initial $1 million noncontrolling investment in </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Competition, Marketing and Customers</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The visiting nurse industry is highly competitive and fragmented.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competitors include larger publicly held companies such as Amedisys,&nbsp;Inc. (NasdaqGS: AMED), Kindred Healthcare,&nbsp;Inc. (NYSE: KND), and LHC Group,&nbsp;Inc. (NasdaqGS: LHCG), and numerous privately held multi-site home care companies, privately held single-site agencies and a significant number of hospital-based agencies. Competition for customers at the local market level is very fragmented and market specific.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, each local market has its own competitive profile and no one competitor has significant market share across all our markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the best of our knowledge, no individual provider has more than 7% share of the national Medicare home health market.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We believe the primary competitive factors are quality of service and reputation among referral sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;We market our services through our site managers and marketing staff.&nbsp;&nbsp;These individuals contact referral sources in their areas to market our services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Major referral sources include: physicians, hospital discharge planners, Offices on Aging, social workers, and group living facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also utilize, to a lesser degree, consumer-direct sales, marketing and advertising programs designed to attract customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The personal care industry is likewise highly competitive and fragmented.&nbsp;&nbsp;Competitors include home health providers, senior adult associations, and the private hiring of caregivers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We market our services primarily through our site </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">11</font>

		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">managers, and we compete by offering a high quality of care and by helping families identify and access solutions for care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Major referral sources include case managers, physicians and hospital discharge planners.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our HCI segment competes in new industries, some of which were created by the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (the &#x201C;ACA&#x201D;), signed into law in March&nbsp;2010.&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain cases, we operate in relatively new and unproven markets which include new competitors that are identified regularly and which range in size from start-up companies to larger publicly held companies like Universal American Corp. (NYSE: UAM).&nbsp;&nbsp;We market our services directly to our customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Government Regulation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Medicare Home Health Program</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Payment Methodology</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As shown in &#x201C;Compensation for Home Health Services&#x201D; above, approximately 68% of our 2016 consolidated net service revenues were derived from the Medicare Home Health Program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare reimburses home health care providers under the Prospective Payment System (&#x201C;PPS&#x201D;), which pays a fixed, predetermined rate for services and supplies under an episode of care.&nbsp;&nbsp;An episode of home health care spans a 60-day period, starting with the first day a billable visit is furnished to a Medicare beneficiary and ending 60 days later.&nbsp;&nbsp;If a patient is still in treatment on the 60</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:6.5pt;">th</font><font style="display:inline;"> day, a new episode begins on the 61</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:6.5pt;">st</font><font style="display:inline;"> day, commonly referred to as a recertification episode, regardless of whether a billable visit is rendered on that day and ends 60 days later.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Payment rates are subject to adjustment based on certain variables including, but not limited to: (a)&nbsp;a case-mix adjustment, which drives the home health resource group (&#x201C;HHRG&#x201D;) to which the Medicare patient is assigned based on such factors as the patient&#x2019;s clinical, functional, and services utilization characteristics; (b)&nbsp;geographic wage adjustment, including rural rate add-ons, if any; (c)&nbsp;a payment adjustment based upon the level of therapy services required (thresholds set at 6, 14 and 20 visits); (d)&nbsp;a low utilization payment adjustment (&#x201C;LUPA&#x201D;) if the number of visits was fewer than five; (e)&nbsp;an outlier payment if our patient&#x2019;s care was unusually costly (capped at 10% of total reimbursement at the agency level); (f)&nbsp;a partial payment if our patient transferred to another provider or we received a patient from another provider before completing the episode; (g)&nbsp;the number of episodes of care provided to a patient; and (h)&nbsp;sequestration, a 2% legislated reduction pursuant to the Budget Control Act (&#x201C;BCA&#x201D;) signed into law on August&nbsp;2, 2011, which was effective for episodes ended after March&nbsp;31, 2013.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In establishing payment rates for the last three years, the Medicare Program recalibrated the national average case-mix levels and maintained budget neutrality by making a corresponding adjustment to the National, Standardized 60-Day Episode Payment Rate (&#x201C;Base Episode Payment Rate&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;These nominal case-mix and payment rate recalibrations result in a lower case mix and higher base rates and are intended to have no effect on payments actually made.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have presented the Base Episode Payment Rate established by the Medicare Program for all episodes of care ended on or after the applicable time periods, along with the Base Episode Payment Rate for each period as if the case-mix resets were in effect for all prior periods below:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">After determining the appropriate PPS payment rate, we record net revenues as services are rendered to patients over the 60-day episode period.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of each month, a portion of our revenue is estimated for episodes that have not yet completed, which are generally referred to as episodes in progress.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, net service revenues recorded for an episode in progress is subject to change if the actual number of visits differs from the number anticipated at the start of care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our revenue recognition under the Medicare reimbursement program is discussed in greater detail in Part&nbsp;II,&nbsp;Item 7 &#x201C;Critical Accounting Policies&#x201D; and Item 8, &#x201C;Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements&#x201D;.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">2017 CMS Related Updates</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On October 31, 2016, CMS issued its CY2017 Home Health Prospective Payment System Rate Update, which includes a 0.7% rate cut consisting of a 2.8% market basket update minus a 0.3% productivity adjustment, a 2.3% rebasing cut, and a 0.97% case mix adjustment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on our initial analysis of the 2017 rule, we estimate it will reduce our Medicare reimbursement rates for 2017 in the range of 1% to 2%.&nbsp; The impact of recalibration of the case-mix model on the Company results in 2017 will depend upon the Company&#x2019;s actual patient mix in that period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Investors are encouraged to read the rule in its entirety at https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/11/03/2016-26290/medicare-and-medicaid-programs-cy-2017-home-health-prospective-payment-system-rate-update-home.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On June 8, 2016, CMS announced the &#x201C;Pre-Claim Review Demonstration of Home Health Services&#x201D; which seeks to demonstrate that a review of selected documentation prior to payment of claims can decrease &#x201C;improper payments because of insufficient documentation&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;According to the CMS announcement, the pre-claim review demonstration will help educate Home Health Agencies (&#x201C;HHA&#x201D;) on what documentation is required and encourage them to submit the correct documentation, while still allowing the HHA to begin providing services and receive initial payments prior to the pre-claim review decision.&nbsp;&nbsp;The pre-claim review demonstration began in Illinois in 2016, Florida is expected to begin April 1, 2017 and Texas, Michigan and Massachusetts will phase in over 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently unable to predict what impact, if any, this demonstration program may have on its result of operations or financial position.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In January of 2017, CMS released a final rule revising the conditions of participation (&#x201C;CoPs&#x201D;) for home health agencies to participate in the Medicare and Medicaid programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The rule is effective July 13, 2017 and focuses on, among other things, care delivered to patients, an interdisciplinary view of patient care, greater flexibility in meeting quality of care standards and the elimination of certain unneeded procedural burdens on providers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are currently unable to predict what impact, if any, this new rule may have on our result of operations or financial position.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Medicaid Reimbursement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As shown in &#x201C;Compensation for Home Health Services&#x201D; above, approximately 23% of our 2016 consolidated net service revenues were derived from state Medicaid and Other Government Programs, with approximately 9.6%, 5.0%, 4.0%, 2.3% and 1.0% generated from Medicaid reimbursement programs in the states of Ohio, Connecticut, New York, Tennessee and Kentucky, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net service revenues under such state programs are derived from services provided under a per visit, per hour or unit basis (as opposed to episodic).&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenues are calculated and recorded using payor-specific or patient-specific fee schedules based on the contracted rates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The financial condition of the Medicaid programs in each of the states in which we operate is cyclical with some currently facing significant budget issues.&nbsp;&nbsp;States may be expected from time to time to take actions or evaluate taking actions to control the rate of growth of Medicaid expenditures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among these actions are the following:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">changing regulations under which providers must operate.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Medicaid programs, while partially federally funded, are administered by the individual states under the broad supervision of CMS.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accordingly, developments typically occur on a state-by-state basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specific programs and changes are enacted regularly.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any such changes, if enacted, could adversely impact our operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Medicare and Medicaid Reimbursement Summary</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The health care industry has experienced, and is expected to continue to experience, extensive and dynamic periods of change.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to economic forces and regulatory influences, continuing political debate subjects the health care </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">industry to significant reform.&nbsp;&nbsp;Health care reforms have been enacted as discussed elsewhere in this document and proposals for additional changes are continuously formulated by departments of the Federal government, Congress, and state legislatures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such governmental payors provide for approximately 91% of our consolidated net service revenues, including Medicare Advantage plans run by private insurers which are also dependent on federal funding.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We expect legislators and government officials to continuously review and assess alternative health care delivery systems and payment methodologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in the law or new interpretations of existing laws may have a dramatic effect on the definition of permissible or impermissible activities, the relative cost of doing business, and the methods and amounts of payments for medical care by both governmental and other payors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect legislative changes intended to &#x201C;balance the budget&#x201D; and slow the annual rate of growth of Medicare and Medicaid to continue.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such future changes may further impact reimbursement for our services.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that future legislation or regulatory changes will not have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Governments might take or consider taking further actions because the number of Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries and their related expenditures are growing at a faster rate than the governments&#x2019; revenue.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare and Medicaid are consuming increasing percentages of budgets and may expand further driven by state based exchanges resulting from the ACA and implementing regulations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Health care financing issues are exacerbated when revenues slow in a down economy.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that these financing issues are cyclical in nature rather than indicative of the long-term prospect for Medicare and Medicaid funding of health care services for the populations we serve.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we believe our services offer the lowest cost alternative to institutional care and are a critical part of the solution to our nation&#x2019;s health care financing problems.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Given the broad and far reaching implications of all the changes in the rapidly evolving environment in which we operate, the incomplete nature of these changes, the pace at which the changes are taking place and the prospects for future changes to be made, we cannot predict the ultimate impact, which may be material and adverse, that health care reform efforts and resulting Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement rates will have on our liquidity, our results of operations, the realizability of the carrying amounts of our intangible assets, including goodwill, or our financial condition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, we are unable to predict what effect, if any, such material adverse effect, if it were to occur, might have on our ability to continue to comply with the financial covenants of our revolving credit facility and our ability to continue to access debt capital through that facility.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Permits and Licensure</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Many states require companies providing certain health care services to be licensed as home health agencies. In addition, certain health care practitioners employed by us require state licensure and/or registration and must comply with laws and regulations governing standards of practice.&nbsp;&nbsp;The failure to obtain, renew or maintain any of the required regulatory approvals or licenses could adversely affect our business.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe we are currently licensed appropriately where required by the laws of the states in which we operate.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that either the states or the federal government will not impose additional regulations upon our activities which might adversely affect our results of operations, financial condition, or liquidity.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Certain states require companies providing health care services to obtain a certificate of need issued by a state health-planning agency.&nbsp;&nbsp;Where required by law, we have obtained certificates of need from those states.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain any certificates of need which may be required in the future, if we expand the scope of our services or if state laws change to impose additional certificate of need requirements, and any attempt to obtain additional certificates of need will cause us to incur certain expenses.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Medicare and Medicaid Participation</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Effective March&nbsp;25, 2011, CMS implemented new enrollment regulations which were a response to aspects of the ACA designed to enhance enrollment procedures to protect against fraud.&nbsp;&nbsp;The regulations authorize the establishment of risk categories with risk level dictating the enrollment screening activities, i.e., more rigorous screening as the perceived risk </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">15</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">increases.&nbsp;&nbsp;For Medicare, there are three categories of providers i.e., &#x201C;limited,&#x201D; &#x201C;moderate,&#x201D; or &#x201C;high&#x201D; risk, and CMS has placed newly enrolling home health agencies in the &#x201C;high risk&#x201D; category, with existing enrolled home health agencies categorized as &#x201C;moderate risk.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the low risk provider screening procedures, providers in the moderate risk category will be subject to unannounced site visits. For high risk providers, any individual with a 5% or more ownership interest will be subject to fingerprint-based criminal history record checks.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the new regulations authorize Medicare and state Medicaid agencies to impose temporary enrollment moratoria for a particular type of provider if determined to be necessary to combat fraud, waste, or abuse.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that home health agencies are subject to a moratorium, any newly enrolling home health agency, including any change of ownership subject to the 36 month rule, and any expansion to add a branch would be affected by the moratorium.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Other Regulations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A series of laws and regulations dating back to the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1987 (&#x201C;OBRA 1987&#x201D;) and through the ACA and related subsequent legislation have been enacted and apply to us.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in applicable laws and regulations have occurred from time to time since OBRA 1987 including reimbursement reductions and changes to payment rules.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes are also expected to occur continuously for the foreseeable future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a provider of services under Medicare and Medicaid programs, we are subject to the Medicare and Medicaid anti-kickback statute and other &#x201C;fraud and abuse laws.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;The anti-kickback statute prohibits any bribe, kickback, rebate or remuneration of any kind in return for, or as an inducement for, the referral of Medicare or Medicaid patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may also be affected by the Federal physician self-referral prohibition, known as the &#x201C;Stark&#x201D; law, which, with certain exceptions, prohibits physicians from referring patients to entities in which they have a financial interest or from which they receive financial benefit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Penalties for violations of the federal Stark law include payment sanctions, civil monetary penalties, and/or program exclusion.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many states in which we operate have adopted similar self-referral laws, as well as laws that prohibit certain direct or indirect payments or fee-splitting arrangements between health care providers, if such arrangements are designed to induce or to encourage the referral of patients to a particular provider.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and other legislative and administrative initiatives, Federal and state enforcement efforts against the health care industry have increased dramatically, subjecting all health care providers to increased risk of scrutiny and increased compliance costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We are subject to routine and periodic surveys, audits and investigations by various governmental agencies.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to surveys to determine compliance with the conditions of participation, CMS has engaged a number of contractors (including Fiscal Intermediaries, Recovery Audit Contractors, Program Safeguard Contractors, Zone Program Integrity Contractors, and Medicaid Integrity Contributors) to conduct audits to evaluate billing practices and identify overpayments.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to audits by CMS contractors, individual states are implementing similar programs such as using Medicaid Recovery Audit Contractors.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that we are in material compliance with applicable laws. However, we are unable to predict what additional government regulations, if any, affecting our business may be enacted in the future, how existing or future laws and regulations might be interpreted or whether we will be able to comply with such laws and regulations either in the markets in which we presently conduct, or wish to commence, business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Medicare Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The ACA also established ACOs as a tool to improve quality and lower costs through increased care coordination in the Medicare fee-for-service (&#x201C;FFS&#x201D;) program, also known as &#x201C;Original Medicare.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Medicare FFS program covers approximately 70% of the Medicare recipients or approximately 36 million eligible Medicare beneficiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;ACOs are groups of doctors and other healthcare providers working together to provide high quality services and care for their patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;Provider and beneficiary participation in an ACO is purely voluntary and Medicare beneficiaries retain their current ability to seek treatment from any provider they wish.&nbsp;&nbsp;ACOs are legal entities that contract with CMS for three-year periods.&nbsp;&nbsp;Beneficiaries are assigned to ACOs using an &#x201C;attribution&#x201D; model based on a plurality of services provided by the primary care physician.&nbsp;&nbsp;Beneficiaries still have the right to use any doctor or hospital who accepts Medicare, at any time.&nbsp;&nbsp;In order to receive revenues from CMS under the MSSP, the ACO must meet certain minimum savings rates (i.e. save the federal government money) and meet certain quality measures.&nbsp;&nbsp;More specifically, the ACOs costs of </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">16</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">medical expenses for its members during a relevant measurement year must be below the ACOs benchmark by a minimum amount as established by CMS for such ACO.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">CMS established the MSSP to facilitate coordination and cooperation among providers to improve the quality of care for Medicare FFS beneficiaries and reduce unnecessary costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Eligible providers, hospitals, and suppliers may participate in the MSSP by creating, participating in or contracting with an ACO.&nbsp;&nbsp;The MSSP is designed to improve beneficiary outcomes and increase value of care by (1)&nbsp;promoting accountability for the care of Medicare FFS beneficiaries; (2)&nbsp;requiring coordinated care for all services provided under Medicare FFS; and (3)&nbsp;encouraging investment in infrastructure and redesigned care processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The MSSP will reward ACOs that reduce health care costs below their benchmark while also meeting performance standards on quality of care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the final MSSP rules, Medicare will continue to pay individual providers and suppliers for specific items and services as it currently does under the FFS payment methodologies.&nbsp;&nbsp;MSSP rules&nbsp;require CMS to develop a benchmark for savings to be achieved by each ACO, if the ACO is to receive shared savings or for ACOs that have elected to accept responsibility for losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;An ACO that meets the program&#x2019;s quality performance standards will be eligible to receive a share of the savings to the extent its assigned beneficiary medical expenditures are below its own medical expenditure benchmark provided by CMS.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Insurance Programs and Costs</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">We bear significant risk under our large-deductible workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program and our self-insured employee health program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program, we bear risk up to $400,000 per incident.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">The health care industry has experienced, and is expected to continue to experience, extensive and dynamic periods of change.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to economic forces and regulatory influences, continuing political debate subjects the health care industry to significant reform.&nbsp;&nbsp;Very often, sweeping new legislation is followed by subsequent legislation to address previously unanticipated consequences, or to further define provisions that were too vague to implement based on the language of the original legislation and by legal actions to challenge its constitutionality.&nbsp;&nbsp;In our view, it is reasonable to expect this to occur over the next few years.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (the &#x201C;ACA&#x201D;), signed into law in March&nbsp;2010, has adversely impacted our business and it is reasonable to expect this law and future health care reform law to have an impact on our business in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the broad scope of the ACA and related legislation, the significant changes it will effect in the healthcare industry and society generally, and the complexity of the technical issues it addresses, we are unable to predict, at this time, all the ramifications the ACA, its implementing regulations and future health care reform legislation may have on our business as a health care provider or a sponsor of an employee health insurance benefit plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ACA, its implementing regulations and programmatic guidelines and future health care reform legislation could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations or financial condition in ways not currently anticipated by us.</font>

		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Additionally, we may be unable to take actions to mitigate any or all of the negative implications of the ACA, its implementing regulations or programmatic guidelines and future health care regulation which may result in unfavorable earnings, losses, or impairment charges.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">The current status of Federal and State budgets may have a material adverse effect on our future results of operations and financial condition, as well as our ability to access credit and capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">There can be no assurance that Federal and State governments will be able to operate balanced budgets.&nbsp;&nbsp;While the ultimate outcome of these events cannot be predicted, they may have a material adverse effect on the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Historic economic conditions, stimulus efforts by the Federal government and costly new programs created by <a name="_cp_text_1_31"></a>the ACA have placed significant strain on Federal and state budgets, many of which are in a deficit position.&nbsp;&nbsp;Efforts to reduce spending at the Federal and/or state levels may result in reductions in reimbursement by Medicare, Medicaid and other third-party payors along with tax increases, which may in turn result in decreased revenue growth and a decrease in our profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our contractors and suppliers may also be negatively impacted by these conditions and our ability to provide patient care at a lower cost may diminish and reduce our profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Future disruptions in the credit and capital markets, if any, may restrict our access to capital.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, our ability to incur additional indebtedness to fund acquisitions and operations may be constrained.&nbsp;&nbsp;If the Federal and State budgets&#x2019; conditions deteriorate or do not improve, our results of operations or financial condition could be materially and adversely affected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Our profitability depends principally on the level of government-mandated payment rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reductions in rates, or rate increases that do not cover cost increases, may adversely affect our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">We generally receive fixed payments from Medicare and Medicaid for our services based on the level of care that we </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
