Consequently, if our cost of providing services, which consists primarily of labor costs, is greater than the respective Medicare or Medicaid payment rate, our profitability would be negatively impacted.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on our analysis of Medicare&#x2019;s final regulations for the home health prospective payment system, we expect our Medicare reimbursement rates for home health services provided in 2017 to be between 1% and 2% lower than in 2016.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For example, home health providers, including the Company, have received pre-pay Additional Development Requests (&#x201C;ADR&#x201D;) in addition to Recovery Audit Contractor audits (&#x201C;RAC&#x201D;) from the Palmetto Government Benefits Administration (&#x201C;PGBA&#x201D;) as a result of additional CMS funding allocations to MACs to conduct pre-payment reviews.&nbsp;&nbsp;ADR and RAC audits are both general and focused in nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;The PGBA acts as one of our four fiscal intermediaries, but processes the majority of our claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;We would expect ADR and RAC audits to continue in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;If such ADR or RAC audits result in reimbursement adjustments, we may suffer reduced profitability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, our appeal rights related to such audits may lead to cash flow delays due to significant backlog at the Administrative Law Judge level.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Our success depends significantly on referrals from physicians, hospitals, case managers and other patient referral sources in the communities that our home care agencies serve, as well as on our ability to maintain good relationships with these referral sources.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our referral sources are not contractually obligated to refer home care patients to us and may refer their patients to other providers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our growth and profitability depend on our ability to establish and maintain close working relationships with these patient referral sources and to increase awareness and acceptance of the benefits of home care by our referral sources and their patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will be able to maintain our existing referral source relationships or that we will be able to develop and maintain new relationships in existing or new markets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our loss of, or failure to maintain, existing relationships or our failure to develop new relationships could adversely affect our ability to expand our operations and operate profitably.<a name="_cp_text_1_48"></a> &nbsp;As described further below, our relationships with referral sources are heavily regulated and failure to comply with applicable regulations could have a material adverse effect on our financial position or results of operation.&nbsp; </font>

			<a name="_cp_blt_1_66"></a><a name="_cp_text_1_67"></a><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">the federal Civil Monetary Penalty Law, which prohibits providers from various forms of improper billing and from offering remuneration or other inducements to beneficiaries of federal health care programs to influence the beneficiaries&#x2019; decisions to seek specific governmentally reimbursable items or services or to choose particular providers; and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:18pt;"><p style="width:18pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 17.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">

		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<a name="_cp_blt_1_70"></a><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">in addition to the federal laws, some of the states in which we operate have enacted laws prohibiting certain business relationships between physicians and other providers of healthcare services <a name="_cp_text_1_71"></a>and enacted similar state anti-kickback and false claims laws that may apply to items or services reimbursed by any third-party payor, including commercial insurers.&nbsp; </font></p></td></tr></table></div>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">We currently have contractual relationships with <a name="_cp_text_1_72"></a>current and potential referral sources, including certain physicians who provide medical director and consulting services to our Company<a name="_cp_text_1_73"></a> and joint ventures with hospitals.&nbsp;&nbsp;Many of these physicians <a name="_cp_text_1_74"></a>and hospitals are current or potential referral sources. Although we believe our arrangements currently comply with state and federal anti-kickback and Stark laws, we can</font><font style="display:inline;">not assure you that courts or regulatory agencies will not interpret these laws in ways that will implicate our arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;Violations of <a name="_cp_text_1_78"></a>any existing or future laws and regulations could lead to fines<a name="_cp_text_1_79"></a>, civil or criminal penalties, or sanctions, including under the False Claims Act, <a name="_cp_text_1_80"></a>the termination of our rights to participate in federal and state-sponsored programs that may have a material adverse effect on our operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">If our joint ventures, particularly our relationship with CHS violate the law, our business could be adversely affected.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<a name="_cp_text_1_21"></a><font style="display:inline;">The structures and operations of our joint ventures and our arrangements with hospitals, including CHS, and physicians are required to comply with government laws and regulations, including federal and state anti-kickback and referral laws.&nbsp;&nbsp;While we have structured our joint ventures to comply with many of the criteria for safe harbor protection under the Federal Anti-Kickback Statute, our investments in these joint venture arrangements may not satisfy all elements of the safe harbor requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any of our joint ventures were found to be in violation of federal or state anti-kickback or referral laws, we could be required to restructure or terminate them.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also could be required to repay damages to Medicare and Medicaid based on the amounts we have received pursuant to any prohibited referrals, and we could suffer civil or criminal fines and penalties, including the loss of our licenses to operate and our ability to participate in federal and state health care programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The imposition of any of these penalties could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">If any of our agencies fail to comply with the conditions of participation in the Medicare program, that agency could be terminated from the Medicare program, which would adversely affect our net service revenue and profitability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Each of our home care <a name="_cp_text_1_33"></a>and hospice agencies must comply with the extensive conditions of participation in the Medicare program. If any of our agencies fail to meet any of the Medicare conditions of participation, that agency may receive a notice of deficiency from the applicable state surveyor.&nbsp;&nbsp;If that agency then fails to institute a plan of correction to correct the deficiency within the correction period provided by the state surveyor, that agency could be terminated from the Medicare program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, failure to comply with the conditions of participation related to enrollment could result in a deactivation or revocation of billing privileges.&nbsp;&nbsp;To the extent that billing privileges are revoked, there is a mandated one to three-year bar to re-enrollment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The failure to pass a site verification visit, for example, could result in a revocation of billing privileges with a mandated two-year bar to re-enrollment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the revocation would only immediately affect the particular enrollment subject to the revocation, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (&#x201C;CMS&#x201D;) has indicated that following a revocation it will review the enrollment files for providers under common ownership or control to determine if a similar sanction is warranted for any of the other related providers. <a name="_cp_text_1_34"></a>Similarly, we could face liability under the False Claims Act if we submit claims to Medicare or Medicaid while not in compliance with certain conditions of participation that would cause the government to refuse payment.&nbsp;&nbsp; Any termination of one or more of our home care agencies from the Medicare program for failure to satisfy the program&#x2019;s conditions of participation, including proposed and future amendments could adversely affect our net service revenue and profitability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We may be subject to substantial malpractice or other similar claims.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The services we offer involve an inherent risk of professional liability and related substantial damage awards.&nbsp;&nbsp;On any given day, we have thousands of nurses, therapists and other direct care personnel driving to and from patients&#x2019; homes where they deliver medical and other care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to the nature of our business, we and the caregivers who provide services on our behalf may be the subject of medical malpractice claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;These caregivers could be considered our agents, and, as a result, we could be held liable for their medical negligence.&nbsp;&nbsp;We <a name="_cp_text_1_81"></a>are also subject to claims against us for negligence and intentional misconduct and violations of applicable law, and claims alleging personal injury, assault, abuse, wrongful death, and other charges.&nbsp;&nbsp;Regulatory agencies may initiate administrative proceedings alleging that our services, employees or agents violate applicable laws and seek to impose monetary penalties on us or ask for recoupment of amounts paid.&nbsp;&nbsp;We could be required to incur significant costs to respond to regulatory investigations or defend against lawsuits and, if we do not prevail, we could be required to pay substantial amounts of money in damages, </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Delays in reimbursement may cause liquidity problems.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our business is characterized by delays in reimbursement from the time we provide services to the time we receive reimbursement or payment for these services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Data submission requirements change from time to time for payors, payments to us may be delayed pending additional data or documentation requests by the fiscal intermediary, or our ability to effectively respond to such requirements may delay our payment cycle.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we have information system problems or issues that arise with Medicare or Medicaid, we may encounter delays in our payment cycle. Such a timing delay may cause working capital shortages.&nbsp;&nbsp;Working capital management, including prompt and diligent billing and collection, is an important factor in our results of operations and liquidity.&nbsp;&nbsp;System problems, Medicare or Medicaid issues or industry trends may extend our collection period, adversely impact our working capital.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our working capital management procedures may not successfully negate this risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are often timing delays when attempting to collect funds from Medicaid programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;Delays in receiving reimbursement or payments from these programs may adversely impact our working capital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On June 8, 2016, CMS announced the &#x201C;Pre-Claim Review Demonstration of Home Health Services&#x201D; which seeks to demonstrate that a review of selected documentation prior to payment of claims can decrease &#x201C;improper payments because of insufficient documentation.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;According to the CMS announcement, the pre-claim review demonstration will help educate Home Health Agencies (HHA) on what documentation is required and encourage them to submit the correct documentation, while still allowing the HHA to begin providing services and receive initial payments prior to the pre-claim review decision.&nbsp; The pre-claim review demonstration began in Illinois in late 2016, Florida is expected to begin April 1, 2017 and Texas, Michigan and Massachusetts will phase in over 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently unable to predict what impact, if any, this demonstration program may have on its result of operations or financial position.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">The home health care <a name="_cp_text_1_82"></a>and hospice industry is highly competitive.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our agencies compete with local and regional home health care <a name="_cp_text_1_84"></a>and hospice companies, hospitals, nursing homes, and other businesses that provide home nursing services, some of which are large established companies that have significantly greater resources than we do.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our primary competition comes from local companies in each of our markets, and these privately-owned or hospital-owned health care providers vary by region and market.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete based on the availability of personnel; the quality, expertise, and value of our services; and in select instances, on the price of our services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Increased competition in the future from existing competitors or new entrants may limit our ability to maintain or increase our market share.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will be able to compete successfully against current or future competitors or that competitive pressures will not have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, or results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Some of our existing and potential new competitors may enjoy greater name recognition and greater financial, technical, and marketing resources than we do.&nbsp;&nbsp;This may permit our competitors to devote greater resources than we can to the development and promotion of services.&nbsp;&nbsp;These competitors may undertake more far-reaching and effective marketing campaigns and may offer more attractive opportunities to existing and potential employees and services to referral sources.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We expect our competitors to develop new strategic relationships with providers, referral sources, and payors, which could result in increased competition.&nbsp;&nbsp;The introduction of new and enhanced service offerings, in combination with industry consolidation and the development of strategic relationships by our competitors, could cause a decline in revenue or loss of market acceptance of our services or make our services less attractive.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we compete with a number of non-profit organizations that can finance acquisitions and capital expenditures on a tax-exempt basis or receive charitable contributions that are unavailable to us.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We expect that industry forces will continue to have an impact on our business and that of our competitors.&nbsp;&nbsp;In recent years, the health care industry has undergone significant changes driven by efforts to reduce costs, and we expect these cost containment measures to continue in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Frequent regulatory changes in our industry, including reductions in reimbursement rates and changes in services covered, have increased competition among home health care providers.&nbsp;&nbsp;If we are unable to react competitively to new developments, our operating results may suffer.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Portions of our Healthcare Innovations segment compete in relatively new and developing markets, face larger more well-capitalized competitors and rely on small numbers of relatively large customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Portions of our Healthcare Innovations segment compete in new and developing markets with new competitors or solutions developed and introduced to the market regularly.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such new products may capture market share more quickly or may have access to more capital than the capital we have allocated for such projects.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our efforts to bring new solutions to the market may prove unsuccessful, may prove to be unprofitable or may prove to be costlier to bring to market than anticipated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our investments in these activities are highly speculative in nature and subject to loss.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, our Ingenios assessment subsidiary competes with larger, better capitalized competitors and our LTS assessment subsidiary is particularly reliant on a small number of large customers, the loss of which could significantly and adversely impact its results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">A shortage of qualified registered nursing staff, physical therapists, occupational therapists and other caregivers could adversely affect our ability to attract, train and retain qualified personnel and could increase operating costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We rely significantly on our ability to attract and retain caregivers who possess the skills, experience, and licenses necessary to meet the requirements of our patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;We compete for personnel with other providers of health care services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to attract and retain caregivers depends on several factors, including our ability to provide these caregivers with attractive assignments and competitive benefits and salaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;We cannot assure you that we will succeed in any of these areas.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, there are occasional shortages of qualified healthcare personnel in some of the markets in which we operate.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, we may face higher costs of attracting caregivers and providing them with attractive benefit packages than we originally anticipated, and if that occurs, our profitability could decline.&nbsp;&nbsp;Finally, although this is currently not a significant factor in our existing markets, if we expand our operations into geographic areas where healthcare providers have historically unionized, we cannot assure you that the negotiation of collective bargaining agreements will not have a negative effect on our ability to timely and successfully recruit qualified personnel.&nbsp;&nbsp;Generally, if we are unable to attract and retain caregivers, the quality of our services may decline, and we could lose patients and referral sources.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Risks Related to Our Business</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We depend on government sponsored reimbursement programs with Medicare accounting for the largest portion of our revenues.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">For the years ended December 30, 2016, January 1, 2016 and December&nbsp;31, 2014, we received 68%, 71% and 72%, respectively, of our revenue from Medicare.&nbsp; Reductions in Medicare reimbursement have historically and may continue to adversely impact our profitability. Such reductions in payments to us could be caused&nbsp;by:</font>
		</p>

Our largest Medicaid reimbursement is concentrated in the states of Ohio, Connecticut, New York, Tennessee and Kentucky.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Part II, Item 8, Note 1, &#x201C;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&#x201D; elsewhere in this Form 10-K for further details.</font>

Medicaid is consuming a greater percentage of states&#x2019; budgets.&nbsp;&nbsp;This issue is exacerbated when revenues slow in a slowing economy.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is possible that the actions taken by the federal government or state Medicaid programs in the future could have a significant unfavorable impact on our results of operations, financial condition and liquidity.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Migration of our Medicare beneficiary patients to Medicare managed care providers could negatively impact our operating results.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Historically, we have generated a substantial portion of our revenue from the Medicare fee-for-service market.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Congress continues to allocate significant additional funds and other incentives to Medicare managed care providers in order to promote greater participation in those plans by Medicare beneficiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;If these increased funding levels have the intended result, the size of the potential Medicare fee-for-service market could decline, thereby reducing the size of our potential patient population, which could cause our operating results to suffer.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Our business plan calls for significant growth in our business over the next several years.&nbsp;&nbsp;This growth will place significant demands on our management and information technology systems, internal controls, and financial and professional resources.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, we will need to further develop our financial controls and reporting systems to accommodate future growth.&nbsp;&nbsp;This could require us to incur expenses for hiring additional qualified personnel, retaining professionals to assist in developing the appropriate control systems, and expanding our information technology infrastructure.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our inability to manage growth effectively could have a material adverse effect on our financial results.</font>

(&#x201C;LTS&#x201D;), a provider of in-home nursing assessments for the long-term care insurance industry for a purchase price of $37 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;These investments are highly speculative and are at risk and we may choose to make further investments, all of which may ultimately provide no return and could lead to a total loss of our investment.&nbsp; </font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">We face additional federal <a name="_cp_text_1_90"></a>and state requirements in the transmission and retention and protection of health information.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (&#x201C;HIPAA&#x201D;) was enacted to ensure that employees can retain and at times transfer their health insurance when they change jobs and to simplify healthcare administrative processes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The enactment of HIPAA expanded protection of the privacy and security of personal medical data and required the adoption of standards for the exchange of electronic health information.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among the standards that the Secretary of <a name="_cp_text_1_91"></a>the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has adopted pursuant to HIPAA are standards for electronic transactions and code sets, unique identifiers for providers, employers, health plans and individuals, security and electronic signatures, privacy and enforcement. <a name="_cp_text_1_93"></a>We are subject to HIPAA as a covered entity.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<a name="_cp_text_1_95"></a><font style="display:inline;">HIPAA was amended by the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act <a name="_cp_text_1_96"></a>of 2009 (&#x201C;HITECH Act&#x201D;), <a name="_cp_text_1_98"></a>which set forth health information security breach notification requirements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The HITECH Act requires patient notification for all breaches<a name="_cp_text_1_99"></a> related to Protected Health Information, media notification of breaches of over 500 patients and at least annual reporting of all breaches to the Secretary of HHS.&nbsp;&nbsp;The HITECH Act<a name="_cp_text_1_101"></a>, as amended by the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Improvements Act of 2015, provides for sanctions for violations of HIPAA and HITECH of up to $1,650,300 per year for each violation. A single breach incident can result in violation of multiple standards, resulting in maximum possible penalties in excess of $1,650,300. HIPAA mandates that the Secretary of HHS conduct periodic compliance audits, which could result in penalties if we become subject to an audit and are found not to be in compliance with our obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Failure to comply with <a name="_cp_text_1_102"></a>HIPAA, HITECH<a name="_cp_text_1_103"></a>, and state privacy and security laws could result in fines and penalties <a name="_cp_text_1_104"></a>or civil liability that could have a material adverse effect on us.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">We bear significant insurance risk under our large-deductible workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program and our self-insured employee health program.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also carry D&amp;O coverage for potential claims against our directors and officers, including securities actions. &nbsp;Claims made to date or in the future may exceed the limits of such insurance, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such claims, if successful and in excess of such limits, could have a material adverse effect on our ability to conduct business or on our assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;Benefits provided by our employer sponsored health insurance plan may require changes as a result of the ACA or other regulatory action.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such changes may have an adverse impact on our operating results.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Laws and regulations governing the Medicare and Medicaid programs are extremely complex and subject to interpretation.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is common for issues to arise related to: (1) medical coding, particularly with respect to Medicare, (2) patient eligibility, particularly related to Medicaid, and (3) other reasons unrelated to credit risk, all of which may result in adjustments to recorded revenue amounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management continuously evaluates the potential for revenue adjustments and when appropriate provides allowances for losses based upon the best available information.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is at least a reasonable possibility that recorded estimates could change by material amounts in the near term.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">ITEM 7.&nbsp;&nbsp;MANAGEMENT&#x2019;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSI<a name="ITEM7MANAGEMENTSDISCUSSIONANDANALYSIS_57"></a>S OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">OVERVIEW</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has two divisions, Home Health care and Healthcare Innovations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Home Health care division is comprised of two reportable segments, Visiting Nurse Services (&#x201C;VN&#x201D; or &#x201C;Visiting Nurse&#x201D;) and Personal Care Services (&#x201C;PC&#x201D; or &#x201C;Personal Care&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our Healthcare Innovations division is also a reporting segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reportable segments have been identified based upon how management has organized the business by services provided to customers and the criteria in ASC Topic 280, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Segment Reporting</font><font style="display:inline;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our VN segment provides skilled medical services in patients&#x2019; homes largely to enable recipients to reduce or avoid periods of hospitalization and/or nursing home care.&nbsp;&nbsp;VN Medicare revenues are generated primarily on a per episode basis rather than a fee per visit or an hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated 70% of our revenue for 2016 with approximately 95% generated from the Medicare program while the balance is generated from Medicaid and private insurance programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our PC segment services are also provided in patients&#x2019; homes.&nbsp;&nbsp;These services (generally provided by paraprofessional staff such as home health aides) are generally of a custodial rather than skilled nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;PC revenues are generated primarily on an hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated 26% of our revenue for 2016 with approximately 83% generated from Medicaid and other government programs while the balance is generated from insurance programs and private pay patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our HCI business segment was created to house and separately report on its developmental activities outside our traditional home health business platform.&nbsp;&nbsp;These activities are intended ultimately, whether directly or indirectly, to benefit patients and payers through the enhanced provision of home health services.&nbsp;&nbsp;HCI&#x2019;s activities all share a common goal of improving patient experiences and quality outcomes, while lowering costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;These include, but are not limited to: technology, information, population health management, risk-sharing, assessments, care coordination and transitions, clinical advancements, enhanced patient engagement and informed clinical decision making.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe these activities help us discover valuable insight and experiences that would not otherwise be gained in the routine operation of our core home health business segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, we believe these innovation activities will play an important role in collaborating with policy makers, payers, providers, and anyone who assumes financial risk for managing patient populations, to seek to reduce costs and improve quality by providing increasingly more care for more patients in their homes than ever before.&nbsp;&nbsp;This segment generated approximately 4% of our revenue for 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The HCI segment now includes: a)&nbsp;Imperium Health Management,&nbsp;LLC ("Imperium"), an ACO enablement company, b)&nbsp;Long Term Solutions,&nbsp;Inc. ("LTS"), an in-home assessment company serving the long-term care insurance industry, c)&nbsp;Ingenios Health&nbsp;Co. (&#x201C;Ingenios&#x201D;), a Nurse-Practitioner-oriented and mobile technology-enabled health risk assessment company primarily serving managed care organizations; and d)&nbsp;an investment in NavHealth,&nbsp;Inc. ("NavHealth"), a population-health analytics company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Recent Developments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December&nbsp;31, 2016, the first day after our 2016 fiscal year end, we acquired an 80% controlling interest in the entity holding the home health and hospice assets of Community Health Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (NYSE: CYH) (referred to herein as &#x201C;CHS Home Health&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS Home Health, a provider of skilled home health and hospice services, currently operates 74 home health and 15 hospice branch locations in 22 states.&nbsp;&nbsp;With the completion of this transaction, Almost Family now operates 340 branches across 26 states. &nbsp; &nbsp;The purchase price of $128&nbsp;million was funded through borrowings on the Company's Revolving Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;We expect the transaction will add approximately $200 million in revenue, all of which will be included reported in our Home Health division.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:12pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">2017 Common Stock Offering</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January 25, 2017, we sold 3,450 shares of common stock at $44.50 per share for gross proceeds of approximately $153.5 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total net proceeds, after underwriting discounts and commissions and our offering expenses, were approximately $144.3&nbsp;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;These proceeds were used to repay obligations under the revolving credit facility.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">2015 and 2016 Acquisitions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2016, we completed three acquisitions and increased our ownership of one of our HCI subsidiaries.&nbsp;&nbsp;In the third quarter, one of our HCI subsidiaries redeemed certain outstanding shares increasing our ownership percentage to 72.0% from 61.5%.&nbsp;&nbsp;On June 18, 2016, the Company acquired certain home health agency assets primarily in Wisconsin, but also in Connecticut and Kentucky (collectively, the &#x201C;Wisconsin Acquisition&#x201D;).&nbsp; On January&nbsp;5, 2016, we acquired 100% of the equity of LTS for a purchase price of $37&nbsp;million. On January 5, 2016, we also purchased the assets of a Medicare-certified home health agency owned by Bayonne Visiting Nurse Association (&#x201C;Bayonne&#x201D;) located in New Jersey.&nbsp;&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During 2015, we completed four acquisitions and made a cost based investment.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November 5, 2015, we completed the acquisition of Black Stone Operations, LLC (&#x201C;Black Stone&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Black Stone owned and operated personal care and skilled home health services in western Ohio.&nbsp;&nbsp;On August 29, 2015, we completed the acquisition of Bracor, Inc. (dba &#x201C;WillCare&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;WillCare owned and operated VN and PC branch locations in New York (12) and Connecticut (1).&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 1, 2015 we acquired the stock of WillCare&#x2019;s Ohio operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 22, 2015, we acquired Ingenios Health Co.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ingenios is a leading provider of technology enabled in-home clinical assessments for Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial Exchange lives in 7 states and Washington, D.C.&nbsp;&nbsp;The results of the Black Stone and WillCare acquisitions are reported in our VN and PC segments, while our Ingenios acquisition results are included in the Healthcare Innovations segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January&nbsp;29, 2015, we acquired a noncontrolling interest in a development stage analytics and software company, NavHealth.&nbsp;&nbsp;The investment is an asset of our Healthcare Innovations segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Our View on Reimbursement and Diversification of Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our Company is highly dependent on government reimbursement programs which pay for the majority of the services we provide to our patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;Reimbursement under these programs, primarily Medicare and Medicaid, is subject to frequent changes as policy makers balance their own needs to meet the health care needs of constituents while also meeting their fiscal objectives.&nbsp;&nbsp;Medicare and Medicaid are consuming a greater percentage of federal and states&#x2019; budgets, respectively, which is exacerbated in times of economic downturn.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that these financial issues are cyclical in nature rather than indicative of the long-term prospect for Medicare and Medicaid funding of health care services.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, we believe our services offer the lowest cost alternative to institutional care and is a part of the solution to both balancing the federal budget and the states&#x2019; Medicaid financing problems.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We believe that an important key to our historical success and to our future success is our ability to adapt our operations to meet changes in reimbursement as they occur.&nbsp;&nbsp;One important way in which we have achieved this adaptability in the past, and in which we plan to achieve it in the future, is to maintain some level of diversification in our business mix.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The execution of our business plan will place primary emphasis on the development of our home health operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;As our business grows, we may evaluate opportunities for the provision of other health care services in patients&#x2019; homes that would be consistent with our Senior Advocacy mission.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">37</font>

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Our Business Plan</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our future success depends on our ability to execute our business plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the next three to five years we will try to accomplish the following:</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Health Care Reform Legislation and Medicare Regulations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Federal Government has been pursuing a comprehensive reform of the US healthcare system since early 2009.&nbsp; Numerous changes have been enacted, proposed and continue to be debated, which are discussed in more detail in Part&nbsp;I,&nbsp;Item 1, &#x201C;Government Regulation&#x201D; and Part&nbsp;I,&nbsp;Item 1A, &#x201C;Risk Factors.&#x201D;&nbsp; Many of the change provisions do not take effect for an extended period of time and most will require the publication of implementing regulations and/or the issuance of programmatic guidelines.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">It is reasonable to expect that recent and potential changes described in Part&nbsp;I,&nbsp;Item 1, Government Regulation, might have a more immediate and negative impact on those providers generating lower margins than us, with more leverage relative to earnings than us, with less capital resources than us, or with less ability to adapt their operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe this may result in a contraction of the number of home health providers.&nbsp; In the event of such a contraction in the number of providers, we believe the surviving providers may benefit from a higher rate of admissions growth than would have otherwise occurred.&nbsp; Those surviving providers may earn incremental margins on those higher admissions that may serve to offset a portion of the rate reduction from the Medicare program.&nbsp; However, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in attracting such higher admissions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">It is also reasonable to expect that future rate cuts will present additional opportunities for us to make acquisitions of other providers at valuations and on terms that are attractive to us and enable us to spread our segment and unallocated corporate overhead expenses across a larger business base.&nbsp; However, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in making such acquisitions or that such opportunities will present themselves.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result of the broad scope of health care reform, the significant changes it will effect in the healthcare industry and society generally, and the complexity of the technical issues it addresses, we are unable to predict, at this time, all the ramifications health care reform may have on our business as a health care provider or a sponsor of an employee health insurance benefit plan.&nbsp; These matters could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations or financial condition in ways not currently anticipated by us.&nbsp; This may increase our costs, decrease our revenues, expose us to expanded liability or require us to revise the ways in which we conduct our business.&nbsp; Refer to the results of operations for the impact of these items on revenue, operating and net income for the years ended December 30, 2016, January 1, 2016 and December&nbsp;31, 2014.</font>
		</p>

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We recognize revenues when patient services are provided, primarily in our patients&#x2019; homes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net service revenues are stated at amounts estimated by us to be their net realizable values.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are paid for our services primarily by federal and state third-party reimbursement programs and, to a lesser degree, commercial insurance companies and patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Medicare Episodic Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Approximately 68% of our consolidated net service revenues are derived from the Medicare program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net service revenues are recorded under the Medicare prospective payment program (&#x201C;PPS&#x201D;) based on a 60-day episode payment rate that is subject to adjustment based on certain variables including, but not limited to: (a)&nbsp;changes in the base episode payments established by the Medicare program; (b)&nbsp;adjustments to the base episode payments for case-mix and geographic wages; (c)&nbsp;a low utilization payment adjustment (&#x201C;LUPA&#x201D;) if the number of visits was fewer than five; (d)&nbsp;a partial payment if our patient transferred to another provider or we received a patient from another provider before completing the episode; (e)&nbsp;a payment adjustment based upon the level of therapy services required (thresholds set at 6, 14 and 20 visits); (f)&nbsp;an outlier payment if our patient&#x2019;s care was unusually costly (capped at 10% of total reimbursement at the agency level); (g)&nbsp;the number of episodes of care provided to a patient; and (h)&nbsp;2% sequestration reduction.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At the beginning of each Medicare episode, we calculate an estimate of the amount of expected reimbursement based on the variables outlined above and recognize Medicare revenue on an episode-by-episode basis during the course of each episode over its expected number of visits.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the course of each episode, as changes in the variables become known, we calculate and record adjustments as needed to reflect changes in expectations for that episode from those established at the start of the 60 day period until its ultimate outcome at the end of the 60 day period is known.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Non-Medicare Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Substantially all remaining revenues are derived from services provided under a per visit, per hour or unit basis (as opposed to episodic) for which revenues are calculated and recorded using payor-specific or patient-specific fee schedules based on the contracted rates in each third party payor agreement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Contingent Service Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our Healthcare Innovations segment provides strategic health management services to ACOs that have been approved to participate in the &#x201C;MSSP.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to having ownership interests in a few ACOs, we also have service agreements with ACOs that provide for sharing of MSSP payments received by the ACO, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;ACOs are entities that contract with Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to serve the Medicare fee-for-service population with the goal of better care for individuals, improved health for populations and lower costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;ACOs share savings with CMS to the extent that the actual costs of serving assigned beneficiaries are below certain trended benchmarks of such beneficiaries and certain quality performance measures are achieved.&nbsp;&nbsp;The MSSP is relatively new and therefore has limited historical experience, which impacts the Company&#x2019;s ability to accurately accumulate and interpret the data available for calculating an ACOs&#x2019; shared savings, if any.&nbsp;&nbsp;MSSP payments are not recognized in revenue until persuasive evidence of an arrangement exists, services have been rendered, the payment is fixed and determinable and collectability is assured, which generally is satisfied only upon cash receipt.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under such agreements, we recognized $4.3 million and $1.4 million in MSSP payments for cash received during 2016 and 2015 related to savings generated for the program period ended December 31, 2015 and December&nbsp;31, 2014, respectively, which accounted for 17% and 41%, respectively of our HCI segment revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;No revenue has been recognized related to potential MSSP payments for savings generated for the program period ended December&nbsp;31, 2016, if any.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue Adjustments</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Laws and regulations governing the Medicare and Medicaid programs are extremely complex and subject to interpretation.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, we may adjust previously recorded revenue amounts due to issues related to: a) medical coding, particularly with respect to Medicare, b) patient eligibility, particularly with respect to Medicaid, and c) other reasons unrelated to credit risk.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue adjustments, if any, to reflect actual payment amounts for completed episodes </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">40</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">or services provided under per visit, per hour or unit basis which differ from our estimates or audit adjustments are recorded when known and estimable.&nbsp;&nbsp;Historically, revenue adjustments have not been significant and as such, we believe that net service revenues and accounts receivable - net reflect their net realizable value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in estimates related to prior periods (increased) decreased revenues by approximately ($608,000), ($365,000) and ($320,000) in the years ended December 30, 2016, January 1, 2016 and December&nbsp;31, 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Accounts Receivable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Accounts receivable are reported at their estimated net realizable value and are net of estimated allowances for uncollectible accounts and adjustments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable consist primarily of amounts due from third-party payors and patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;We evaluate the collectability of our accounts receivable based on certain factors, such as payor types, historical collection trends and aging categories.&nbsp;&nbsp;We calculate our reserve for uncollectible accounts based on the length of time that the receivables are past due.&nbsp;&nbsp;The percentage applied to the receivable balances for each payor&#x2019;s various aging categories is based on historical collection experience, business and economic conditions and reimbursement trends.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Insurance Programs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We bear significant risk under our large-deductible workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program and our self-insured employee health program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program, we bear risk up to $400,000 per incident.&nbsp;&nbsp;We purchase stop-loss insurance for the employee health plan that places a specific limit, generally $300,000, on our exposure for any individual covered life.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Malpractice and general patient liability claims for incidents which may give rise to litigation have been asserted against us by various claimants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The claims are in various stages of processing and some may ultimately be brought to trial.&nbsp;&nbsp;We are aware of incidents that have occurred through year-end that may result in the assertion of additional claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;We currently carry professional and general liability insurance coverage (on a claims made basis) for this exposure with no deductible.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also carry D&amp;O coverage (also on a claims made basis) for potential claims against our directors and officers, including securities actions, with deductibles ranging from $175,000 to $500,000 per claim.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We record estimated liabilities for our insurance programs based on information provided by the third-party plan administrators, historical claims experience, the life cycle of claims, expected costs of claims incurred but not paid, and expected costs to settle unpaid claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;We monitor our estimated insurance-related liabilities and recoveries, if any, on a monthly basis and as required by ASU 2010-24, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Health Care Entities (Topic 954): Presentation of Insurance Claims and Related Insurance Recoveries,</font><font style="display:inline;"> record amounts due under insurance policies in other current assets, while recording the estimated carrier liability in other current liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;As facts change, it may become necessary to make adjustments that could be material to our results of operations and financial condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Intangible assets are stated at fair value at the time of acquisition and goodwill represents the excess cost over the fair value of net assets acquired and liabilities assumed.&nbsp;&nbsp;Finite lived intangible assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful life of the asset. Goodwill and indefinite-lived assets are not amortized.&nbsp;&nbsp;We perform impairment tests of goodwill and indefinite lived assets as required by ASC Topic 350,&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Intangibles - Goodwill and Other</font><font style="display:inline;"> on at least an annual basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment analysis requires numerous subjective assumptions and estimates to determine fair value of the respective reporting units.&nbsp;&nbsp;We estimate the fair value of the related reporting units using a combined market approach (guideline company and similar transaction method) and income approach (discounted cash flow analysis).&nbsp;&nbsp;These models are based on our projections of future revenues and operating costs and are reconciled to our consolidated market capitalization.&nbsp;&nbsp;Discounted cash flow models are highly reliant on various assumptions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant assumptions we utilize in these models for the current year included:&nbsp;&nbsp;projected business results and future industry direction, long-term growth factor of 3% and weighted-average cost of capital of 15%.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use assumptions that we deem to be reasonable estimates of likely future events and compares the total fair values of each reporting unit to our overall market capitalization, and implied control premium, to determine if the fair values are reasonable compared to </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">41</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">external market indicators.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent changes in these key assumptions could affect the results of future goodwill impairment reviews.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Important to our overall impairment conclusion was the comparison of the aggregate fair values of the reporting units to our overall market capitalization at the annual assessment date, including the implied control premium, to determine if the fair values are reasonable compared to external market indicators.&nbsp;&nbsp;The aggregate fair value for each reporting unit did not exceed our market value as of the annual impairment testing date.&nbsp;&nbsp;A negative control premium indicates conservatism built into our fair value models.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Because the fair value results for each reporting unit did not indicate a potential impairment existed, we did not recognize any goodwill or intangible asset impairment during 2016, 2015 and 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically, our VN, PC and HCI reporting unit fair values were significantly over their carrying value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on the sensitivity analysis performed on two key assumptions in the discounted cash flow models of each reporting unit, a 100 basis point change in either assumption (either individually or in the aggregate) would not result in any impairment of our goodwill or intangible assets within either reporting unit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Assuming no changes in the key assumptions identified and projected results, we currently anticipate the future fair value of our reporting units to increase over time; however, future declines in the operating results of either reporting unit could indicate a need to reevaluate the fair value of these businesses under U.S. GAAP requirements and may ultimately result in an impairment to goodwill. We will continue to monitor for any potential indicators of impairment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We account for taxes in accordance with ASC Topic 740,&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font><font style="display:inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016, we have net deferred tax liabilities of approximately $21.1 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net deferred tax liability is composed of approximately $18.9 million of deferred tax assets and approximately $40.0 million of deferred tax liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have provided a valuation allowance against certain deferred tax assets based upon our estimates of realizability of those assets through future taxable income.&nbsp;&nbsp;This valuation allowance was based in large part on our history of generating operating income or losses in individual tax locales and expectations for the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our ability to generate the expected amounts of taxable income from future operations is dependent upon general economic conditions, competitive pressures on revenues and margins and legislation and regulation at all levels of government.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, we have book goodwill of $105.1 million which is not deductible for tax purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;The remaining deductible goodwill provides an annual tax deduction approximating $15.2 million through 2022.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have considered the above factors in reaching our conclusion that it is more likely than not that future taxable income will be sufficient to fully utilize the deferred tax assets (net of the valuation allowance) as of December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<div style="width:100%"><table style="width:100%;" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0"><tr><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td valign="top" align="left" style="width: 18.00pt; display: inline;">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
				<font style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size:10pt;;"> (1)</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:0pt;"><p style="width:0pt;width:0pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">Percentages pertain to percentage of total admissions or total billable visits, as applicable.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">VN segment net service revenues increased $35.1 million or 8.8% to a record $436.1 million in 2016 primarily due to acquisitions occurring late in 2015 (WillCare and Black Stone) and in 2016 (Bayonne).&nbsp;&nbsp;Acquisitions drove increases in Medicare billable visits, Medicare admissions and Medicare recertifications, which increased 7.3% to 2,537,873, 4.0% to 95,487 and 6.1% to 51,731, respectively in 2016.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Substantially all of the changes in cost of service revenues, general and administrative expenses and payor information were due to acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Gross margin as a percentage of revenue decreased to 51.1% from 51.6% primarily due to higher labor costs per visit from acquired agencies and higher insurance claims experience.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total general and administrative expenses declined slightly as a percentage of revenue to 38.1% from 39.2% in 2015 primarily from the effect of acquired operations plus the closure of selected underperforming branches in late 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result, VN segment operating income before corporate expenses improved $6.7 million to $56.6 million from $49.8 million in the prior year, while VN segment operating income as a percentage of revenue increased to 13.0% from 12.4% in the prior year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Personal Care Segment-Years Ended December 30, 2016 and January&nbsp;1, 2016</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">PC segment net revenue increased $33.7 million or 26.4% to a record $161.4 million due to acquisitions in the second half of 2015 (WillCare and Black Stone) and in mid-2016 (Wisconsin).&nbsp; Cost of service revenues as a percentage of net service revenues increased slightly to 69.0% in 2016 from 67.8% in 2015 due to the mix of acquired operations and rate reductions in certain skilled elements of the Connecticut and Ohio Medicaid programs.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">Total general and administrative expenses increased as a percent of net service revenues to 22.6% from 21.1% in 2015, largely due to higher insurance claims experience in 2016 as compared to 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result, PC segment operating income before corporate expenses as a percentage of revenue decreased 2.7%, or $0.7 million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
