			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Corporate expenses as a percentage of revenue decreased slightly to 4.9% in 2015 from 5.1% in 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deal, transition and other costs for 2015 include a net benefit of $4.2 million related to legal settlements, which was offset by $2.5 million of deal and transition costs related to our 2015 acquisitions, the $1.8 million provision for the Chapter 7 bankruptcy filing of a specific payor and $1.4 million related to the fourth quarter of 2015 closure of underperforming branch locations in the VN segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deal and transition costs in 2014 primarily related to the completion of the transition of our 2013 acquisitions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense increased $0.6 million due to borrowings on our line of credit in conjunction with 2015 acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our effective tax rate for 2015 was 34.5% compared to 41.0% for 2014.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lower effective tax rate for 2015 was primarily related to the tax treatment of a legal settlement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Excluding the non-taxable settlement and other nondeductible deal costs, our effective tax rate for 2015 would have been 40.5%.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">VN segment net service revenues increased primarily due to the WillCare and Black Stone acquisitions which increased net service revenues by $15.3 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The acquisitions increased operating income before corporate expenses by $3.0 million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Substantially all of the changes in cost of service revenues and general and administrative expenses were due to the WillCare and Black Stone acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Excluding the effects of the WillCare and Black Stone acquisitions, operating income before corporate expenses improved $3.9 million primarily due to higher volumes and an effective Medicare rate increase of about 1%.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Gross margin as a percent of revenue decreased 0.7% primarily due to organic volume growth, the Medicare rate increase and lower cost per visit.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total general and administrative expenses declined slightly as a percentage of revenue to 39.2% from 39.7% in the prior year primarily due to organic volume growth and the Medicare rate increase.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As a result, VN segment operating income before corporate expenses improved to $49.9 million from $42.9 million in the prior year, while VN segment operating income as a percentage of revenue increased to 12.4% from 11.3% in the prior year.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Personal Care Segment-Years Ended January 1, 2016 and December&nbsp;31, 2014</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Approximately 83% of the PC segment revenues were generated from Medicaid and other government programs while the balance is generated from insurance programs and private pay patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;(In thousands, except statistical information)</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">PC segment net revenue increased due to the WillCare and Black Stone acquisitions which increased net service revenues by $15.9 million and operating income before corporate expenses by $2.5 million.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We believe that a certain amount of debt has an appropriate place in our overall capital structure, when reimbursement visibility permits, and it is not our strategy to eliminate all debt financing.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that our cash flow from operations, cash on hand, and borrowing capacity on our bank credit facility, described below, will be sufficient to cover operating needs, future capital expenditure requirements and scheduled debt payments of miscellaneous small borrowing arrangements.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, it is likely that we will pursue growth from acquisitions, partnerships and other ventures that would be funded from excess cash from operations, cash on hand, credit available under the bank credit agreement and other financing arrangements that are normally available in the marketplace.&nbsp;&nbsp;Further, our board may pursue a stock repurchase program or may decide to pay special dividends in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">2017 Common Stock Offering</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January 25, 2017, we sold 3,450 shares of common stock at $44.50 per share for gross proceeds of approximately $153.5 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Total net proceeds, after underwriting discounts and commissions and our offering expenses, were approximately $144.3&nbsp;million.&nbsp;&nbsp;These proceeds were used to repay obligations under the revolving credit facility.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Revolving Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0.05pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December 5, 2016, we entered into a new and expanded revolving credit facility with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent, and certain other lenders (the &#x201C;Facility&#x201D;).&nbsp; The Facility provides a revolving credit facility under which up to $350 million became available upon completion of the CHS JV Transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Facility also includes an &#x201C;accordion&#x201D; feature providing up to $150 million of additional borrowings upon further request and approval by a lender or lenders.&nbsp; Borrowings, other than letters of credit, under the Facility generally will bear interest at a varying rate equal to the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#x201C;LIBOR&#x201D;) plus a margin which varies from 1.50% to 2.75%, depending on our leverage ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Facility is secured by substantially all our assets and the assets and stock of our subsidiaries.&nbsp;Our subsidiaries have also guaranteed the Facility.&nbsp; Debt issuance costs of $4.7 million were capitalized with the Facility and will be amortized through December 5, 2021, the termination date for the Facility.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0.05pt 0pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Borrowings under the Facility are subject to various covenants, including a maximum leverage ratio for all calculation dates ending on or before December&nbsp;31, 2017, of 4.0 times earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, as adjusted (&#x201C;EBITDA&#x201D;) plus &#x201C;Acquired EBITDA&#x201D; from pro-forma acquisitions as defined.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum leverage ratio steps down, to a maximum leverage ratio of 3.75 times EBITDA plus Acquired EBITDA for calculation dates after December&nbsp;31, 2017, and on or before June&nbsp;30, 2018, and to a maximum leverage ratio of 3.5 times EBITDA plus Acquired EBITDA for calculation dates on and after September&nbsp;30, 2018.&nbsp; Borrowings under the Facility may be used for general corporate purposes, including acquisitions.  A portion of the proceeds were used to repay all the outstanding obligations of our prior credit agreement.&nbsp; Additionally, on December 30, we borrowed approximately $128.9 million from the Facility to finance the CHS Home Health Transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;See Part II, Item 8, Note 13, &#x201C;Subsequent Events&#x201D; for further details.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Application of the Facility&#x2019;s borrowing formula as of December 30, 2016, would have permitted approximately $78.6 million to be used; however, after consideration of the pay down from the stock offering on January 25, 2017, approximately $204.1 million of borrowings were available.  &nbsp;As of December 30,&nbsp;2016, we were in compliance with the various financial covenants. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We had irrevocable letters of credit totaling $14.7 million outstanding in connection with our self-insurance programs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effective interest rates on our borrowings were 3.6% and 3.5% for 2016 and 2015, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We believe the Facility will be sufficient to fund our operating needs and expansion plans for at least the next year.&nbsp;&nbsp;We will continue to evaluate additional capital, including possible debt and equity investments in the Company, to support a more rapid development of the business than would be possible with internal funds.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">2016 Compared to 2015</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Net cash provided by operating activities of $24.4 million resulted primarily from current year net income of $17.7 million and the net impact of non-cash and other working capital changes.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of not acquiring accounts receivable in conjunction with our Wisconsin acquisition in June 2016 and normal delays from obtaining applicable licensure approvals, accounts receivable increased $10.2 million without which cash flows from operating activities would have been $34.6 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;Excluding the acquisition related build, accounts receivable days sales outstanding declined 5 days to 53 at December 30, 2016 from 58 at January 1, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;The decline was due to improved collections throughout the home health division, particularly related to previously disclosed backlogs of accounts receivable in Tennessee.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Cash used in investing activities was largely driven by acquisition related activity including the $128.9 million transaction deposit for CHS JV Transaction, $19.7 million for LTS, $6.1 million for Wisconsin, and $4.1 million for Bayonne.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capital expenditures were $6.2 million, up $3.1 million from 2015, primarily related to information systems investments related to our VN segment&#x2019;s conversion to HomeCare HomeBase which began in the fourth quarter of 2016. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Cash provided by financing activities was driven by borrowings on the revolving credit facility, net of repayments from operating cash flows, primarily for acquisitions, along with $3.9 million for debt issuance costs incurred with the new credit facility. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">2015 Compared to 2014</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Net cash provided by operating activities resulted primarily from current period net income of $19.5 million, plus certain non-cash items, net of changes in accounts receivable, accounts payable and accrued expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Accounts receivable days sales outstanding, which were 58 at January 1, 2016 and 55 at December 31, 2014, increasing due to collection delays, primarily in the PC segment, as a result of changes in patient enrollment and billing requirements enacted by the Medicaid managed care providers in Tennessee.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The cash used in investing activities was primarily due to acquisitions, capital expenditures of $3.1 million and a $1.0 million cost basis investment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The cash provided by financing activities resulted from $67.3 million of new borrowings on the revolving credit facility and $1.2 million debt issuance costs incurred in November 2015 in connection with a new five year $175 million credit facility.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

					<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 11pt;">

					<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 11pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Adjusted EBITDA </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Adjusted earnings before interest, income tax, depreciation, amortization, amortization of stock-based compensation, and deal, transition and other (&#x201C;Adjusted EBITDA&#x201D;) is not a measure of financial performance under U.S. GAAP.&nbsp;&nbsp;It should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for net income, operating income, cash flows from operating, investing or financing activities, or any other measure calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.&nbsp;&nbsp;The items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA are significant components in understanding and evaluating financial performance and liquidity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Management routinely calculates and communicates Adjusted EBITDA and believes that it is useful to investors because it is commonly used as an analytical indicator within our industry to evaluate performance, measure leverage capacity and debt service ability, and to estimate current or prospective enterprise value. Adjusted EBITDA is used in certain covenants contained in our revolving credit facility.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Our primary market risk exposure with regard to financial instruments is to changes in interest rates.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">NOTE 1 - SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Basis of Consolidation and Description of Business</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Almost Family,&nbsp;Inc. </font><font style="display:inline;">(a Delaware corporation) and its wholly-owned subsidiaries (collectively &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Almost Family</font><font style="display:inline;">&#x201D; or the &#x201C;Company&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is a leading provider of cost efficient, high quality home healthcare care services and related innovations to drive savings for payors and improve patient outcomes and experience. &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December&nbsp;31, 2016, subsequent to our year-end, the Company acquired an 80% controlling interest in the entity holding the home health and hospice assets of Community Health Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (&#x201C;CHS&#x201D; and &#x201C;CHS Home Health&#x201D; or &#x201C;CHS JV Transaction&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS Home Health, a provider of skilled home health and hospice services, currently operates 74 home health and 15 hospice branch locations in 22 states.&nbsp;&nbsp;With the completion of this transaction, Almost Family now operates 340 branches across 26 states. &nbsp; &nbsp;The purchase price of $128.0 million was funded through borrowings on the Company's Revolving Credit Facility and is included in Transaction Deposit in the Consolidated Balance Sheet at December 30, 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS retained the remaining 20%.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On June 18, 2016, the Company acquired certain home health agency assets primarily in Wisconsin, but also in Connecticut and Kentucky (collectively, the &#x201C;Wisconsin Acquisition&#x201D;).&nbsp; On January&nbsp;5, 2016, the Company acquired 100% of the equity of Long Term Solutions, Inc. (&#x201C;LTS&#x201D;) &nbsp;for a purchase price of $37&nbsp;million.&nbsp; On January 5, 2016, the Company purchased the assets of a Medicare-certified home health agency owned by Bayonne Visiting Nurse Association (&#x201C;Bayonne&#x201D;) located in New Jersey.&nbsp; On November 5, 2015, the Company completed the acquisition of Black Stone Operations, LLC (&#x201C;Black Stone&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Black Stone owned and operated personal care and skilled home health services in western Ohio.&nbsp;&nbsp;On August 29, 2015, the Company completed the acquisition of Bracor, Inc. (dba &#x201C;WillCare&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;WillCare owned and operated Visiting Nurse (&#x201C;VN&#x201D;) and Personal Care (&#x201C;PC&#x201D;) branch locations in New York (12), and Connecticut (1).&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 22, 2015, the Company acquired Ingenios Health (&#x201C;Ingenios&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Ingenios is a leading provider of technology enabled in-house clinical assessments for Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial Exchange lives in four states and Washington, D.C.&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 2, 2015, the Company acquired the stock of WillCare&#x2019;s Ohio operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 29, 2015, the Company acquired a noncontrolling interest in a development stage analytics and software company, NavHealth, Inc. (&#x201C;NavHealth&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The acquisitions are more fully described in Note 11, &#x201C;Acquisitions.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#x201C;US GAAP&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;All intercompany balances and transactions have been eliminated. </font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Fiscal Year End</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Effective with the first quarter of 2015, the Company adopted a 52-53 week fiscal reporting calendar under which it will report its annual results going forward in four equal 13-week quarters.&nbsp;&nbsp;Every fifth year, one quarter will include 14 weeks and that year will include 53 weeks of operating results.&nbsp;&nbsp;All references herein for the years 2016, 2015 and 2014 represent the fiscal years ended December 30, 2016 and January 1, 2016, and the calendar year ended December 31, 2014, respectively.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">New Accounting Pronouncements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In August 2016, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#x201C;FASB&#x201D;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#x201C;ASU&#x201D;) 2016-15, Statement of Cash Flows, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Classification of Certain Cash Receipts and Cash Payments </font><font style="display:inline;">(&#x201C;ASU 2016-15&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-15 clarifies how entities should classify certain cash receipts and cash payments on the statement of cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;It also clarifies how the predominance principle should be applied when cash receipts and cash payments have aspects of more than one class of cash flows.&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-15 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2017, </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">58</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">and interim periods within those years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early adoption is permitted.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact ASU 2016-15 will have on its consolidated financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In March 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-09, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Compensation &#x2013; Stock Compensation </font><font style="display:inline;">(</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;">ASU 2016-09&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-09 is intended to simplify several aspects of the accounting for share-based payments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance will be effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2016, including interim periods within that year.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is in the process of evaluating the impact of the adoption of this ASU.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In February 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-02, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Leases </font><font style="display:inline;">(</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">&#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;">ASU 2016-02&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;ASU 2016-02 requires lessees to recognize assets and liabilities on their balance sheet related to the rights and obligations created by most leases, while continuing to recognize expenses on their income statements over the lease term.&nbsp;&nbsp;It will also require disclosures designed to give financial statement users information regarding the amount, timing, and uncertainty of cash flows arising from leases.&nbsp;&nbsp;The guidance is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2018, and interim periods within those years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Early adoption is permitted for all entities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is currently evaluating the impact ASU 2016-02 will have on its consolidated financial statements and associated disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In April 2015, the FASB issued ASU No. 2015-03, Interest &#x2013; Imputation of Interest (&#x201C;Subtopic 835-30&#x201D;):&nbsp; </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Simplifying the Presentation of Debt Issuance Costs</font><font style="display:inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;In certain instances, Subtopic 835-30 requires that debt issuance costs related to a recognized debt liability be presented in the balance sheet as a direct deduction from the carrying amount of that debt liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subtopic 835-30 is effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;With the adoption of Subtopic 835-30, amortization of debt issuance costs of $281 and $190 were reclassified from amortization expense to interest expense for the years-ended January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2014, respectively, while interest expense for the fiscal year ended December 30, 2016 includes $336 of debt issue costs amortization.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In April 2015, the FASB issued ASU No. 2015-05, Intangibles &#x2013; Goodwill and Other &#x2013; Internal-Use Software (&#x201C;Subtopic 350-40&#x201D;): </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Customer&#x2019;s Accounting for Fees Paid in a Cloud Computing Arrangement</font><font style="display:inline;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subtopic 350-40 provides guidance that all software licenses included in cloud computing arrangement be accounted for consistent with other licenses of intangible assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, if a cloud computing arrangement does not include a software license, the arrangement should be accounted for as a service contract, the accounting for which did not change.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subtopic 350-40 is effective for annual and interim periods beginning after December 15, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The adoption of ASU No. 2015-05 did not affect the Company&#x2019;s financial position and results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">In May 2014, the FASB issued ASU No. 2014-09, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</font><font style="display:inline;"> (&#x201C;Topic 606&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Topic 606 affects virtually all aspects of an entity&#x2019;s revenue recognition, including determining the measurement of revenue and the timing of when it is recognized for the transfer of goods or services to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Topic 606 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is continuing to evaluating Topic 606, but does not initially foresee a material impact from the adoption of Topic 606 on its 2018 financial position and results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Cash and Cash Equivalents</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company considers all highly liquid debt instruments purchased with an original maturity of three months or less to be cash equivalents.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Uninsured deposits at December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016 and January&nbsp;1,&nbsp;2016 were approximately $7,845 and $4,681, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;These amounts have been deposited with national financial institutions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Property and Equipment</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Property and equipment are stated at cost.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation is computed using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives (generally two to ten years for medical and office equipment and three years for internally developed software).&nbsp;&nbsp;Leasehold improvements are depreciated over the terms of the respective leases (generally three to ten years). Such costs are periodically reviewed for recoverability when impairment indicators are present.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such indicators include, among other factors, operating losses, unused capacity, market value declines and technological obsolescence.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recorded values of asset groups of property, plant and equipment that are not expected to be recovered through undiscounted </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">59</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">future net cash flows are written down to current fair value, which generally is determined from estimated discounted future net cash flows (assets held for use) or net realizable value (assets held for sale).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Goodwill and indefinite lived intangible assets acquired are stated at fair value at the date of acquisition.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to acquisition, the Company conducts annual reviews for impairment, or more frequently if circumstances indicate impairment may have occurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company reviews goodwill for impairment based on its identified reporting units, which are the same as its reportable segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company tests goodwill for impairment by comparing the carrying value to the estimated fair value of its reporting units, determined using a combination of the market approach (guideline company</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;">similar transaction method) and income approach (discounted cash flow analysis).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company annually tests its indefinite-lived intangible assets, principally trade names, certificates of need, provider numbers and licenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Specifically trade names are tested using a &#x201C;relief-from-royalty&#x201D; valuation method compared to the carrying value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant assumptions inherent in the valuation methodologies for goodwill and other intangibles are employed and include, but are not limited to, such estimates as future projected business results, growth rates, legislated changes in payment rates, weighted-average cost of capital for a market participant, royalty and discount rates</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">.</font><font style="display:inline;"> &nbsp;The Company has completed its most recent annual impairment tests as of December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016 and determined that no impairment existed.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Finite-lived intangible assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, such as the cost of non-compete agreements for which their estimated useful life is usually 3 years, beginning after the earn-out period, if any.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Capitalization Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Maintenance, repairs and minor replacements are charged to expense as incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;Major renovations and replacements are capitalized to appropriate property and equipment accounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;Upon sale or retirement of property, the cost and related accumulated depreciation are eliminated from the accounts and the related gain or loss is recognized in the consolidated statement of income.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company capitalizes the cost of internally developed computer software for the Company&#x2019;s own use.&nbsp;&nbsp;Software development costs of approximately $1,279, $788 and $327 were capitalized in the years ended December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016, January&nbsp;1, 2016 and December 31, 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Insurance Programs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company bears significant risk under its large-deductible workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program and its self-insured employee health program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the workers&#x2019; compensation insurance program, the Company bears risk up to $400 per incident, after which stop-loss coverage is maintained.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company purchases stop-loss insurance for the employee health plan that places a specific limit, generally $300, on its exposure for any individual covered life.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Malpractice and general patient liability claims for incidents which may give rise to litigation have been asserted against the Company by various claimants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The claims are in various stages of processing and some may ultimately be brought to trial.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company currently carries professional and general liability insurance coverage (on a claims made basis) for this exposure with no deductible.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also carries D&amp;O coverage (also on a claims made basis) for potential claims against the Company&#x2019;s directors and officers, including securities actions, with deductibles ranging from $175 to $500 per claim.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company records estimated liabilities for its insurance programs based on information provided by the third-party plan administrators, historical claims experience, the life cycle of claims, expected costs of claims incurred but not paid, and expected costs to settle unpaid claims.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company monitors its estimated insurance-related liabilities and recoveries, if any, on a monthly basis and records amounts due under insurance policies in other current assets, while recording the estimated carrier liability in other current liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;As facts change, it may become necessary to make adjustments that could be material to the Company&#x2019;s results of operations and financial condition.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Income Taxes</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company recognizes deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that have been included in the financial statements or tax returns.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under this method, deferred tax assets and liabilities are determined based on the difference between the Company&#x2019;s book and tax bases of assets and liabilities and tax carry-</font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">61</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">forwards using enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which the differences are expected to reverse.&nbsp;&nbsp;The effect of changes in tax rates on deferred taxes is recognized in the period in which the enactment dates change.&nbsp;&nbsp;Valuation allowances are established when necessary on a jurisdictional basis to reduce deferred tax assets to the amounts expected to be realized.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Noncontrolling Interest Redeemable</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company acquired a controlling interest in Imperium in October of 2013 and currently owns 72.0%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is party to a put and call arrangement with respect to the remaining 28.0% non-controlling interest in Imperium.&nbsp;&nbsp;The redemption value for both the put and the call arrangement is equal to fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to the existing put and call arrangements, the noncontrolling interest is considered to be redeemable and is recorded on the balance sheet as a redeemable noncontrolling interest outside of permanent equity.&nbsp;&nbsp;The redeemable noncontrolling interest is recognized at the higher of 1) the accumulated earnings associated with the noncontrolling interest or 2) the redemption value as of the balance sheet date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Seasonality</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s VN segment operations located in Florida (which generated approximately 26% of that segment&#x2019;s revenues in the year ended December 30, 2016) normally experience higher admissions during the first quarter and lower admissions during the third quarter than in the other quarters due to seasonal population fluctuations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Net Service Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company is paid for its services primarily by federal and state third-party reimbursement programs, commercial insurance companies, and patients. Revenues are recorded at established rates in the period during which the services are rendered.&nbsp;&nbsp;Appropriate allowances to give recognition to third party payment arrangements are recorded when the services are rendered.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Approximately 68% of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated net service revenues are derived from the Medicare program.&nbsp;&nbsp;Net service revenues are recorded under the Medicare prospective payment program (PPS) based on a 60-day episode payment rate that is subject to adjustment based on certain variables including, but not limited to: (a)&nbsp;changes in the base episode payments established by the Medicare program; (b)&nbsp;adjustments to the base episode payments for case-mix and geographic wages; (c)&nbsp;a low utilization payment adjustment (LUPA) if the number of visits was fewer than five; (d)&nbsp;a partial payment if a patient is transferred to another provider or if a patient is received from another provider before completing the episode; (e)&nbsp;a payment adjustment based upon the level of therapy services required (thresholds set at 6, 14 and 20 visits); (f)&nbsp;an outlier payment if the patient&#x2019;s care was unusually costly (capped at 10% of total reimbursement); (g)&nbsp;the number of episodes of care provided to a patient; and (h)&nbsp;a 2% reduction for sequestration.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At the beginning of each Medicare episode the Company calculates an estimate of the amount of expected reimbursement based on the variables outlined above and recognizes Medicare revenue on an episode-by-episode basis during the course of each episode over its expected number of visits.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the course of each episode, as changes in the variables become known, adjustments are calculated and recorded as needed to reflect changes in expectations for that episode from those established at the start of the 60 day period until its ultimate outcome at the end of the 60 day period is known.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Substantially all remaining revenues are earned on a per visit, hour or unit basis (as opposed to episodic).&nbsp;&nbsp;For all services provided, the Company uses either payor-specific or patient-specific fee schedules for the recording of revenues at the amounts actually expected to be received.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Laws and regulations governing the Medicare and Medicaid programs are extremely complex and subject to interpretation.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is common for issues to arise related to: 1) medical coding, particularly with respect to Medicare, 2) patient eligibility, particularly related to Medicaid, and 3) other reasons unrelated to credit risk, all of which may result in adjustments to recorded revenue amounts.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company continuously evaluates the potential for revenue adjustments and when appropriate provides allowances for losses based upon the best available information.&nbsp;&nbsp;There is at least a </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">62</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">reasonable possibility that recorded estimates could change by material amounts in the near term.&nbsp;&nbsp;Changes in estimates related to prior periods (increased) decreased revenues by approximately ($608), ($365), and ($320) in 2016, 2015 and 2014, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Revenue and Receivable Concentrations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The following table sets forth the percent of the Company&#x2019;s revenues generated from Medicare, state Medicaid programs and other payors for the year ended:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Contingent Service Revenues</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company, through its Imperium acquisition, provides strategic health management services to ACOs that have been approved to participate in the Medicare Shared Savings Program (&#x201C;MSSP&#x201D;).&nbsp; In some cases, the Company also had ownership interests in ACOs beginning January 1, 2015.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">ACOs are entities that contract with CMS to serve the Medicare fee-for-service population with the goal of better care for individuals, improved health for populations and lower costs.&nbsp; ACOs share savings with CMS to the extent that the actual costs of serving assigned beneficiaries are below certain trended benchmarks of such beneficiaries and certain quality performance measures are achieved.&nbsp; The MSSP is relatively new and therefore has limited historical experience, which impacts the Company&#x2019;s ability to accurately accumulate and interpret the data available for calculating an ACO&#x2019;s shared savings, if any.&nbsp; MSSP payments are not recognized in revenue until persuasive evidence of an agreement exists, services have been rendered, the payment is fixed and determinable and collectability is insured, which is generally satisfied upon cash receipt.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under such agreements, the Company recognized $4.3 million and $1.4 million in MSSP payments for cash received during 2016 and 2015 related to savings generated for the program period ended December 31, 2015 and December 31, 2014, respectively, which is included in the Company&#x2019;s Healthcare Innovations segment revenues.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has yet to recognize potential MSSP payments, if any, for savings generated for the December&nbsp;31, 2016 program period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Stock options and restricted stock are granted under various stock compensation programs to employees and independent directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company accounts for such grants in accordance with ASC Topic 718, </font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Compensation &#x2014; Stock Compensation</font><font style="display:inline;"> and amortizes the fair value of awards, after estimated forfeiture, on a straight-line basis over the requisite service periods.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Accounting for Leases</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company accounts for operating leases using the straight-line rents method, which amortizes contracted total rents due evenly over the lease term.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">NOTE 4 - REVOLVING CREDIT FACILITY</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December&nbsp;5, 2016, the Company entered into a new and expanded revolving credit facility with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A., as Administrative Agent, and certain other lenders (the &#x201C;Facility&#x201D;).&nbsp; The Facility provides a credit line of $225.0 million on and after December&nbsp;5, 2016, and up to $350 million on and after the closing of the Company&#x2019;s acquisition of 80% of the membership interests in the CHS JV Transaction.&nbsp; The Facility also includes an accordion feature providing that up to $150 million of additional borrowings may be available upon our further request and approval by a lender or lenders willing to extend such borrowings.&nbsp; Borrowings, other than letters of credit, under the Facility generally will bear interest at a varying rate equal to the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#x201C;LIBOR&#x201D;) plus a margin which varies from 1.50% to 2.75%, depending on our leverage ratio.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Facility is secured by substantially all our assets and the assets and stock of our subsidiaries.&nbsp;Our subsidiaries have also guaranteed the Facility.&nbsp; The Facility has a maturity date of December&nbsp;3, 2021.&nbsp;&nbsp;Debt issuance costs of $4.7 million were capitalized with the Facility and will be amortized through December, 2021.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Borrowings under the Facility are subject to various covenants, including a maximum leverage ratio for all calculation dates ending on or before December&nbsp;31, 2017, of 4.0 times earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, as adjusted (&#x201C;EBITDA&#x201D;) plus &#x201C;Acquired EBITDA&#x201D; from pro-forma acquisitions as defined.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum leverage ratio steps down, to a maximum leverage ratio of 3.75 times EBITDA plus Acquired EBITDA for calculation dates after December&nbsp;31, 2017, and on or before June&nbsp;30, 2018, and to a maximum leverage ratio of 3.5 times EBITDA plus </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">66</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">Acquired EBITDA for calculation dates on and after September&nbsp;30, 2018.&nbsp; Borrowings under the revolving credit facility may be used for general corporate purposes, including acquisitions.&nbsp;&nbsp;A portion of the proceeds were used to repay all the outstanding obligations of our prior credit agreement.&nbsp; Additionally, on December 30, 2016 the Company borrowed approximately $128.9 million from the Facility to finance the CHS Home Health transaction, which was classified as a Transaction Deposit and included in Revolving credit facility in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 30, 2016, the Company was in compliance with the various financial covenants.&nbsp;&nbsp;Application of the Facility&#x2019;s borrowing formula as of December 30, 2016, would have permitted approximately $78.6 million to be used.&nbsp;&nbsp;We had irrevocable letters of credit totaling $14.7 million in connection with our self-insurance programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January 25, 2017, the Company sold 3,450 shares of common stock for net proceeds of $144.3&nbsp;million, after deducting the estimated underwriting discounts and commissions and our offering expenses, which were used to repay obligations under the Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, credit available under the Facility increased thereafter to approximately $204&nbsp;million. </font><font style="display:inline;color:#000000;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">See Note 13, &#x201C;Subsequent Events&#x201D; for further details. &nbsp; &nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The effective interest rates on our borrowings were 3.6% and 3.5% for 2016 and 2015, respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">NOTE 5 - FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENTS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s financial instruments consist of cash, accounts receivable, payables and debt instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to their short-term nature, the book values of cash, accounts receivable and payables are considered representative of their respective fair values.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of the Company&#x2019;s debt instruments approximates their carrying values as substantially all of such debt instruments have rates which fluctuate with changes in market rates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016, the Company does not have any assets or liabilities carried at fair value that are measured on a recurring basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has provided a valuation allowance against certain net deferred tax assets based upon management&#x2019;s estimation of realizability of those assets through future taxable income.&nbsp;&nbsp;This valuation allowance was based in large part on the Company&#x2019;s history of generating operating income or losses in individual tax locales and expectations for the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s ability to generate the expected amounts of taxable income from future operations to realize its recorded net deferred tax assets is dependent upon general economic conditions, competitive pressures on revenues and margins and legislation and regulation at all levels of government.&nbsp;&nbsp;There can be no assurances that the Company will </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 30, 2016, the Company has U.S. operating loss carry forwards of $8.1 million that are available to reduce future taxable income.&nbsp;&nbsp;If not used to offset taxable income, the losses will expire between 2028 and 2034.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to U.S. limitations on acquired operating losses, a valuation allowance has been established on $0.8 million of these losses.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">State operating loss carryforwards totaling $42.9 million at December&nbsp;30, 2016 are being carried forward in jurisdictions where the Company is permitted to use tax losses from prior periods to reduce future taxable income.&nbsp;&nbsp;If not used to offset future taxable income, these losses will expire between 2017 and 2036.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to uncertainty regarding the Company&#x2019;s ability to use some of the carryforwards, a valuation allowance has been established on $35.8 million of state net operating loss carryforwards.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on the Company&#x2019;s historical record of producing taxable income and expectations for the future, the Company has concluded that future operating income will be sufficient to give rise to taxable income sufficient to utilize the remaining state net operating loss carryforwards.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">US GAAP prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for the accounting and financial statement disclosure of tax positions taken or expected to be taken in a tax return.&nbsp;&nbsp;The evaluation of a tax position is a two-step process.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first step requires the Company to determine whether it is more likely than not that a tax position will be sustained upon examination based on the technical merits of the position.&nbsp;&nbsp;The second step requires the Company to recognize in the financial statements each tax position that meets the more likely than not criteria, measured at the amount of benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s unrecognized tax benefits would affect the tax rate, if recognized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company includes the full amount of unrecognized tax benefits in other noncurrent liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company anticipates it is reasonably possible an increase or decrease in the amount of unrecognized tax benefits could be made in the next twelve months. 		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Employee Stock Incentive Plans</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has a 2000 Employee Stock Option Plan which initially provided for options to purchase up to 1,000 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock to key employees, officers and directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Board of Directors determines the amount and terms of the options, which cannot exceed ten years.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December&nbsp;30, 2016, options for 83 shares were outstanding under this plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are no shares available for future grant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The 2007 Stock and Incentive Compensation Plan provided for stock awards up to 500 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock to employees, non-employee directors or independent contractors, with a maximum number of full value restricted share awards up to 200.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December&nbsp;30, 2016, options for 230 shares were outstanding under this plan, while 162 restricted shares had been awarded.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are no shares available for future grant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The 2013 Stock and Incentive Compensation Plan provides for stock awards up to 700 shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock to employees, non-employee directors or independent contractors.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December&nbsp;30, 2016, options awarded and outstanding under this plan were 190 and 188, respectively, and restricted shares awarded and outstanding were 296 and 213, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are 214 shares available for future grant.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Historically, the Company has issued restricted share and/or option awards to employees and non-employee directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Board of Directors determines the amount and terms of the options, which cannot exceed ten years.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under both the 2013 and 2007 Stock and Incentive Compensation Plans, restricted share awards cliff vest on the third anniversary, while option share awards vest annually in 25% increments over four years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On March 4, 2016, the Company granted 56 performance-based, restricted share awards (&#x201C;performance shares&#x201D;) under the 2013 Stock and Incentive Compensation Plans to key executives.&nbsp;&nbsp;These performance shares entitle certain executives to receive a number of shares of our common stock based upon the Company&#x2019;s satisfaction of certain performance criteria approved by the Board of Directors.&nbsp;&nbsp;The awards cliff-vest at the end of three years and were valued at the market price of a share of the Company&#x2019;s stock on the date of grant assuming 100% achievement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the plan, achievement ranges from 0% to 200%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company deemed achievement not probable at December 30, 2016 and recorded no compensation expense.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">Expected volatility is based on an analysis that looks at the unbiased standard deviation of the Company&#x2019;s common stock over the option term.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected life of the options represents the period of time that the Company expects the options granted to be outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free rate is based on the U.S. Treasury yield curve in effect at the time of the grant of the option for the expected term of the instrument.&nbsp;&nbsp;A 0% dividend yield was assumed as no dividend payout over the term of the award is expected.</font>
