		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Legal Proceedings </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">From time to time, the Company is subject to various legal actions arising in the ordinary course of the Company&#x2019;s business, including claims for damages for personal injuries.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the Company&#x2019;s opinion, after discussion with legal counsel, the ultimate resolution of any of these pending ordinary course claims and legal proceedings will not have a material effect on the Company&#x2019;s financial position or results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company has complied with a civil subpoena from the United States Department of Justice received in January of 2016 related to two locations acquired along with SunCrest in late 2013.&nbsp;&nbsp;SunCrest had previously acquired the locations in its merger with Omni Home Health in 2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The subpoena seeks the production of various pre-acquisition business records limited to certain Omni operations in Sarasota and Tampa, Florida for the years 2007-2011.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is cooperating fully with this investigation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The subject operations generated less than 1% of the Company&#x2019;s consolidated revenues.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">NOTE 10 - SEGMENT DATA</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">At December&nbsp;30,&nbsp;2016, the Company has two divisions, Home Health care and Healthcare Innovations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Home Health care division is comprised of two reportable segments, Visiting Nurses Services (&#x201C;VN&#x201D; or &#x201C;Visiting Nurse&#x201D;) and Personal Care Services (&#x201C;PC&#x201D; or &#x201C;Personal Care&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Healthcare Innovations is also a reportable segment.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Consistent with information given to the chief operating decision maker, the Company does not allocate certain corporate expenses to the reportable segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;These expenses are included in Unallocated below.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company evaluates the performance of its business segments based on operating income.&nbsp;&nbsp;Intercompany and intersegment transactions have been eliminated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Segment information within the consolidated financial statements have been recast for all periods presented to conform with the new segment reporting structure.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s VN segment provides skilled medical services in patients&#x2019; homes largely to enable recipients to reduce or avoid periods of hospitalization and/or nursing home care.&nbsp;&nbsp;VN Medicare revenues are generated on a per episode basis rather than a fee per visit or day of care.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 95% of the VN segment revenues are generated from the Medicare program, while the balance is generated from Medicaid and private insurance programs. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s PC segment services are also provided in patients&#x2019; homes.&nbsp;&nbsp;These services (generally provided by paraprofessional staff such as home health aides) are generally of a custodial rather than skilled nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;PC revenues are generated on an hourly basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 83% of the PC segment revenues are generated from Medicaid and other government programs, while the balance is generated from insurance programs and private pay patients.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s Healthcare Innovations business segment was created to house and separately report on our developmental activities outside the traditional home health business platform.&nbsp;&nbsp;These activities are intended ultimately, whether directly or indirectly, to benefit the Company&#x2019;s patients and payers through the enhanced provision of home health services.&nbsp;&nbsp;The activities all share a common goal of improving patient experiences and quality outcomes while lowering costs.&nbsp;&nbsp;They include, but are not limited to, items such as: technology, information, population health management, risk-sharing, care coordination and transitions, clinical advancements, enhanced patient engagement and informed clinical decision.</font>
		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:underline;">NOTE 11 - ACQUISITIONS</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company completed each of the following acquisitions in pursuit of its strategy for operational expansion in the eastern United States through an expanded service base and enhanced position in certain geographic areas.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price of each acquisition was determined based on the Company&#x2019;s analysis of comparable acquisitions, expected cash flows and arm&#x2019;s length negotiation with the sellers.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each acquisition was included in the Company&#x2019;s consolidated financial statements from the respective acquisition date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Goodwill recognized from the acquisitions primarily relates to expected contributions of each entity to the overall corporate strategy in addition to synergies and acquired workforce, which are not separable from goodwill.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill and other intangible assets generated in asset purchase transactions are expected to be amortizable for tax purposes on a straight-line basis over 15 years, unless otherwise noted.&nbsp;&nbsp;Goodwill and other intangible assets generated in stock purchase transactions are not amortizable, unless otherwise noted.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During the third quarter of 2016, one of the Company&#x2019;s HCI subsidiaries redeemed certain outstanding shares increasing the Company's ownership percentage to 72.0% from 61.5%.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On June 18, 2016, the Company acquired certain home health agency assets primarily in Wisconsin, but also in Connecticut and Kentucky (collectively, the Wisconsin acquisition).&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price was $6.1 million, funded through borrowings on the Company&#x2019;s bank credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The post-acquisition operating results of these agencies are primarily reported in the Company&#x2019;s PC segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;No accounts receivable were acquired.&nbsp;&nbsp;Thus, accounts receivable need to accumulate to normal levels post close.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January 5, 2016, the Company acquired 100% of the equity of LTS.&nbsp;&nbsp;LTS is a provider of in-home nursing assessments for the long-term care insurance industry.&nbsp;&nbsp;LTS provides assessments in all 50 U.S. states and a number of foreign countries.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price of $37 million was funded through borrowings on the Company&#x2019;s bank credit facility, seller notes and issuance of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects goodwill from this transaction to be deductible for tax purposes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Approximately 74.4% of LTS&#x2019;s 2016 revenue was from two customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;LTS&#x2019;s post acquisition operating results are reported in our Healthcare Innovations business segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On January 5, 2016, the Company purchased the assets of a Medicare-certified home health agency owned by Bayonne located in New Jersey.&nbsp;&nbsp;Bayonne&#x2019;s post acquisition operating results are reported in our VN segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 5, 2015, the Company acquired the stock of Black Stone Operations, LLC (&#x201C;Black Stone&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Black Stone is a provider of in-home personal care and skilled home health services in western Ohio and operates under the name &#x201C;Home Care by Black Stone&#x201D;.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price of $40 million was funded through borrowings on the Company&#x2019;s bank credit facility, seller notes and issuance of the Company&#x2019;s common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects goodwill from this transaction to be deductible for tax purposes.  Black Stone&#x2019;s post acquisition operating results are reported in the Company&#x2019;s VN and PC segments and Healthcare Innovations segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On August 29, 2015, the Company acquired 100% of the equity of Bracor, Inc. (dba &#x201C;WillCare&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;WillCare, based in Buffalo, NY, owned and operated VN and PC branch locations in New York (12) and Connecticut (1).&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price was approximately $50.8 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;The transaction was funded by borrowings under the Company&#x2019;s bank credit facility.&nbsp; WillCare&#x2019;s post acquisition operating results are reported in the Company&#x2019;s VN and PC segments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On July 22, 2015, the Company acquired 100% of the equity of Ingenios Health Co. for approximately $11.4 million of the Company&#x2019;s common stock plus $2 million in cash.&nbsp;&nbsp;Ingenios is a leading provider of technology enabled in-home clinical assessments for Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial Exchange lives in four states and Washington, D.C.&nbsp;&nbsp;The post-acquisition operating results of Ingenios are reported in the Company&#x2019;s Healthcare Innovations business segment.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On March 1, 2015, the Company acquired the stock of WillCare&#x2019;s Ohio operations for $3.0 million.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On December&nbsp;31, 2016, the first day of the Company&#x2019;s 2017 fiscal year, the Company acquired an 80% controlling interest in the entity holding the home health and hospice assets of Community Health Systems,&nbsp;Inc. (NYSE: CYH) (&#x201C;CHS Home Health&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;With the completion of this transaction, the Company now operates 340 branches across 26 states. &nbsp; &nbsp;The purchase price of $128.0 million was funded through borrowings on the Company's Revolving Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS retained the remaining 20%. </font>

("CHS") is one of the largest publicly-traded hospital companies in the United States and a leading operator of general acute care hospitals in communities across the country.&nbsp;&nbsp;CHS Home Health, which includes the former home health and hospice operations of CHS, provides in-home outpatient care services, including skilled nursing and acute care. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The consolidated financial statements appearing in this Annual Report have been prepared by management that is responsible for their preparation, integrity and fair presentation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The statements have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles, which requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended).&nbsp;&nbsp;Our internal control system was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance with respect to financial statement preparation and presentation. Further, because of changes in conditions, the effectiveness of an internal control system may vary over time.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Principal Financial Officer (PFO), we conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December 30, 2016 based on the framework in</font><font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;"> Internal Control &#x2014; Integrated Framework</font><font style="display:inline;"> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (COSO) with the exception of the operations of Long Term Solutions, Inc., which constituted 6% of total assets as of December 30, 2016 and 2% of net service revenues for the&nbsp;&nbsp;fiscal year then ended.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on that evaluation, our management concluded our internal control over financial reporting was effective based on the criteria described above as of December 30, 2016.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, has audited and reported on the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;The report of Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young LLP is contained in this Annual Report.</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:9pt;">Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">The Board of Directors and Stockholders of Almost Family,&nbsp;Inc. and Subsidiaries</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;punctuation-wrap:hanging;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">We have audited Almost Family, Inc. and Subsidiaries&#x2019; internal control over financial reporting as of December 30, 2016, based on criteria established in Internal Control&#x2014;Integrated Framework issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (2013 framework) (the COSO criteria). Almost Family, Inc. and Subsidiaries&#x2019; management is responsible for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting included in the accompanying &#x201C;Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting&#x201D;. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audit.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects. Our audit included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk, and performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of the company&#x2019;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">As indicated in the accompanying Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting, management&#x2019;s assessment of and conclusion on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting did not include the internal controls of Long Term Solutions, Inc., which is included in the 2016 consolidated financial statements of Almost Family, Inc. and Subsidiaries and constituted 6% of total assets as of December 30, 2016 and 2% of net service revenues for the year then ended. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting of Almost Family, Inc. and Subsidiaries also did not include an evaluation of the internal control over financial reporting of Long Term Solutions, Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">In our opinion, Almost Family, Inc. and subsidiaries maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 30, 2016, based on the COSO criteria.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 9pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:9pt;">We also have audited, in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States), the consolidated balance sheets of Almost Family Inc. and Subsidiaries as of December 30, 2016 and January 1, 2016 and the related consolidated statements of income, stockholders&#x2019; equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 30, 2016 and our report dated March 14, 2017 expressed an unqualified opinion thereon.</font>
		</p>

(referred to herein as &#x201C;CHS Home Health&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;With the completion of this transaction, the Company now operates 340 branches across 26 states.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price of $128 million was funded through borrowings on the Company's newly expanded $350 million revolving credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 25, 2017, the Company sold 3,450,000 shares of common stock in a public offering for net proceeds of $144.3 million, after deducting the estimated underwriting discounts and commissions and our offering expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;These proceeds were used to repay obligations under the revolving credit facility, resulting in borrowing capacity of approximately $200 million now available for future growth and acquisitions.</font>

Yarmuth, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, (ii) $375,000 for C. Steven Guenthner, President and Principal Financial Officer, and (iii) $175,000 for P. Todd Lyles, Senior Vice President - Administration.</font>
